https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Temmin_.description: Temmin "Snap" Wexley went from teenage junk dealer to one of the most dependable wingmen in the Resistance, and he fought in the battles that ended both the Empire and the First Order. His father was taken by the Empire and his mother Norra left to fly for the Rebellion, so Temmin grew up on his own in Myrra. He ran a scrap shop out of the family home, did business with local gangsters, and rebuilt a battle droid, Mister Bones, into his fiercely loyal bodyguard. When Norra came home after Endor, the two reconciled during the uprising that freed Akiva from Imperial control. Temmin then joined her team as they hunted Imperial war criminals, learned to fly under Wedge Antilles (who later became his stepfather), and helped free Chewbacca and other prisoners from Ashmead's Lock, where he found his father again. The reunion ended badly when Brentin, controlled by an Imperial implant, took part in the Liberation Day attack on Chandrila. Temmin fought at the Battle of Jakku and went on to serve as a New Republic pilot. Decades later he joined the Resistance, flew with Black Squadron, and became a captain and recon specialist in Blue Squadron at Takodana and Starkiller Base. He married fellow pilot Karé Kun and helped rebuild the Resistance after Crait. He was killed in the Battle of Exegol, and Poe Dameron remembered him as the best wingman he ever had.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Temmin_.socialDesc: Temmin "Snap" Wexley, Akiva junk dealer turned Resistance recon pilot, fought at Jakku and Starkiller Base before dying in the Battle of Exegol.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Temmin_.timeline:
11 BBY - Birth on Akiva

Born to Norra and Brentin Lore Wexley and raised in the city of Myrra.

~5 BBY - Father arrested

Imperial forces arrest Brentin for carrying messages for the Rebel Alliance, and Temmin loses his father while still a young child.

~1 ABY - Mother joins the Rebellion

At about twelve, Temmin is left with his aunt Esmelle and her wife Shirene when Norra leaves Akiva to become a Rebel pilot. He soon moves back into the family home to live on his own.

~2 ABY - Junk dealer and Mister Bones

Turns the family house into a spare-parts shop, gets involved with the gangster Surat Nuat, and rebuilds a B1 battle droid into his bodyguard, Mister Bones.

3 ABY - Meets Kay Vess

After Surat's gang robs him, Temmin makes a deal with the outlaw Kay Vess: he fits a hydro-repulsor to her speeder in exchange for the durasteel struts she recovers from the gang.

4 ABY - Reunion with Norra

After Endor, Norra comes back to Akiva. Temmin is still bitter that she left, but he is pulled into the fight when Surat's thugs capture him and Jas Emari and Sinjir Rath Velus rescue him.

4 ABY - Rebellion on Akiva

Helps seize an Imperial communications station and broadcast a call to revolt. He secretly tries to trade his companions to Surat for safe passage, is betrayed and thrown from the Satrap's palace, then redeems himself by freeing his mother and friends aboard the Golden Harp. Akiva is liberated and joins the New Republic.

4 ABY - Joins the hunt for Imperials

Reconciles with Norra on Chandrila, joins her team to track down Imperial war criminals, and begins flight training under Wedge Antilles.

5 ABY - Capture of Perwin Gedde

Flies the getaway ship Halo on Vorlag and shoots down two pursuing TIE fighters. Wedge offers him a future place in Phantom Squadron.

5 ABY - Rescue at Ashmead's Lock

Joins Han Solo to storm Golas Aram's compound on Irudiru, then helps free Chewbacca and the other prisoners from the automated prison on Kashyyyk. Among the freed prisoners is his father Brentin.

5 ABY - Attack on Chandrila

Uncovers the Imperial agent Windom Traducier but is stunned and hidden by his implant-controlled father. On Liberation Day he confronts Brentin during the assassination attempt on Mon Mothma and stops him from turning the gun on himself.

5 ABY - Hunt for Rae Sloane

Goes with Norra's team across the galaxy looking for Grand Admiral Sloane. After the capture of Mercurial Swift, the trail leads to Jakku.

5 ABY - Battle of Jakku

Fights in the battle that ends the Galactic Empire.

~5 ABY - New Republic pilot

Joins the New Republic Defense Fleet as a starfighter pilot and later serves in the New Republic's precision air team.

~34 ABY - Joins the Resistance

Is recruited into the Resistance and flies in Poe Dameron's Black Squadron alongside Karé Kun.

34 ABY - Battle of Takodana

As a captain in Blue Squadron, flies in the Resistance strike that relieves Takodana.

34 ABY - Destruction of Starkiller Base

Briefs the Resistance on Starkiller Base's defenses and flies in the attack that destroys it.

34 ABY - Rebuilding the Resistance

Is away on a mission during the evacuation of D'Qar and Crait. Afterwards he helps rebuild the Resistance, including recruiting on Corellia.

35 ABY - Kijimi

Takes part in the Resistance operation that rescues the heroes' allies on Kijimi.

35 ABY - Death at the Battle of Exegol

Is killed while flying in the Resistance fleet against the Sith Eternal at Exegol. Poe Dameron later delivers his eulogy.

birth.source: Wookieepedia infobox and biography: born 11 BBY on Akiva.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: died 35 ABY on Exegol during the Battle of Exegol (The Rise of Skywalker; A Eulogy for Snap).

notes.current: Episode VII: The Force Awakens; Episode IX: The Rise of Skywalker

notes.detail: Wookieepedia's infobox uses an image from Star Wars Outlaws, set in 3 ABY, where a teenage Temmin appears as an Akiva junk dealer who helps Kay Vess. The rest of his early life comes from the Aftermath novel trilogy.

notes.suggested: Add Spouse: Karé Kun; Stepfather: Wedge Antilles
notes.detail: The Wookieepedia infobox lists Karé Kun as his spouse and Wedge Antilles as his stepfather. These family links are notable and connect to other characters already on the timeline.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jango_F.description: Jango Fett was the most feared bounty hunter of the Republic's last years, and the man whose DNA became the Grand Army of the Republic. After his parents were murdered, the Mandalorians took him in as a foundling. He trained under a mentor named Jaste, received his own armor and fought in the Mandalorian Civil Wars. He then left to work as a bounty hunter. Over many years he built his reputation with jobs like the Phaedra hunt for Jabba the Hutt and the search for the stolen Hope of Glee Anselm. He also stole the Firespray patrol craft that became Slave I and mentored the young Cad Bane. Soon after the Invasion of Naboo, Darth Tyranus chose him as the clone template on Kamino. His price was twenty million credits and one unaltered clone, whom he raised as his son Boba and taught the family trade. Ten years later he hired Zam Wesell for the plot to kill Senator Padmé Amidala. When she failed, he silenced her with a saberdart, and that dart led Obi-Wan Kenobi to Kamino and then to Geonosis. Jango died in the First Battle of Geonosis in 22 BBY. He shot down Jedi Master Coleman Trebor, but Mace Windu beheaded him. His legacy lived on in the millions of clones who carried out Order 66 and in Boba, who took over his ship and armor and became the galaxy's top bounty hunter in his turn.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jango_F.socialDesc: Jango Fett, the galaxy's top bounty hunter and a Mandalorian foundling, became the clone army's template and died at Mace Windu's hands on Geonosis.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jango_F.timeline:
66 BBY - Birth

Jango Fett is born. He is later tied to the Mandalorian colony world of Concord Dawn, though he likes to keep his true origins vague.

~55 BBY - Mandalorian Foundling

After his parents are murdered, the Mandalorians find the boy on Concord Dawn and take him in as a foundling. They raise him as a warrior, and he trains under a mentor known as Jaste.

~50 BBY - Mandalorian Civil Wars

Jango fights in the Mandalorian Civil Wars and receives his own set of Mandalorian armor.

~45 BBY - Turns to Bounty Hunting

He leaves the Mandalorians to become a bounty hunter. It takes him years of work to build a reputation that lets him pick his own jobs.

~40 BBY - Slave I

On a job at the prison moon Oovo 4, Jango steals a Firespray-31 patrol craft. He names it Slave I and fits it with heavy weapons, including seismic charges.

~40 BBY - Underworld Connections

He works often with the Clawdite Zam Wesell, becomes friends with the pirate Hondo Ohnaka, knows Aurra Sing and mentors the young Cad Bane.

Between 40 and 34 BBY - The Phaedra Job

Jabba the Hutt hires Jango to recover the thief Phaedra and the money she took from the Galactic Bank of Coruscant. On Malastare he makes a deal with her instead, helping her escape Marshal Buck Vancto for three times Jabba's fee.

~33 BBY - The Hope of Glee Anselm

Jango is hired to track the thieves who stole the Hope of Glee Anselm. On Nar Shaddaa he fights off a k'lor'slug, and the case brings him to Count Dooku's attention.

~32 BBY - Recruited by Tyranus

Soon after the Invasion of Naboo, Jango wins a competition set up by Dooku. On the moons of Bogden, Darth Tyranus hires him as the genetic template for the clone army being grown on Kamino.

~32 BBY - Boba Fett

On top of his twenty-million-credit fee, Jango asks for one unaltered clone. He names the boy Boba and raises him as his son in Tipoca City.

32–22 BBY - Overseeing the Clones

Jango helps design the clones' training programs and oversees their flash training. He takes no pride in the troopers and calls them livestock bred as cannon fodder.

32–22 BBY - Training Boba

Jango keeps taking bounties and uses them to teach Boba to pilot, survive, shoot and fight.

~22 BBY - Mission to Ord Mantell

On Boba's first mission, father and son join three hunters to bring back a runaway Twi'lek girl. When Rinn and Tiver betray them, Boba kills both and chooses to spare Neelda.

~22 BBY - The Wesell Run

Jango helps Zam Wesell capture the indebted collector Sinvatt Bovic on Fytoun. During the job he kills a Clawdite imposter and survives a bluebarb wasp dart.

22 BBY - Plot Against Amidala

Working for Dooku, Jango hires Wesell to kill Senator Padmé Amidala. After her attempts fail and the Jedi catch her, he kills her with a Kamino saberdart so she cannot name him.

22 BBY - Confronted on Kamino

Obi-Wan Kenobi questions Jango in Tipoca City and then fights him on the landing platform. Jango escapes to Geonosis with Boba, not knowing Kenobi has put a homing beacon on Slave I.

22 BBY - Chase Through the Asteroids

Jango hunts Kenobi through the Geonosian asteroid field and wrongly believes he has destroyed him.

22 BBY - Death on Geonosis

Jango captures Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala in the droid factory and guards Dooku in the arena. He kills Jedi Master Coleman Trebor, but after a reek tramples him and damages his jetpack, Mace Windu beheads him. Boba mourns over his father's helmet.

birth.source: Wookieepedia, Jango Fett: infobox born field and Early life section both say he was born in 66 BBY.

death.source: Wookieepedia, Jango Fett: infobox gives 22 BBY on Geonosis. Mace Windu beheads him in the First Battle of Geonosis in Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones.

notes.current: Episode II: Attack of the Clones
notes.suggested: Add The Clone Wars, if we list archive or flashback appearances
notes.detail: The Clone Wars Season 2 episode 'Death Trap' opens with Boba remembering Jango's death on Geonosis, which reuses footage of Jango. This is from memory, not from the Wookieepedia text supplied (its Appearances list was cut off), so check it before adding. Only add it if our seenIn policy counts flashback or archive footage.

Wookieepedia says Jango was a Mandalorian foundling, confirmed in The Mandalorian 'Chapter 14: The Tragedy'. This settles the older canon debate over whether the Fetts were Mandalorians, and our entry does not track it at all.

Concord Dawn matches Wookieepedia. However, the article notes that Jango only claimed to come from there, that his exact history stayed unknown, and that Almec disowned any link between him and Mandalore. No change needed; just be aware of it.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Gial_Ac.description: Gial Ackbar was the admiral who commanded the rebel fleet at Endor, the man who saw the Emperor's trap for what it was, and one of the few commanders to serve through every major war from the Clone Wars to the First Order's rise. He started out as Coral City's representative on the Calamari Council and rose to captain of the Mon Calamari Guard. In the Clone Wars he protected the young Prince Lee-Char and guided him through the Separatist-backed civil war on his homeworld, which ended with Lee-Char crowned king. When the Empire invaded Mon Cala, Ackbar led his people's defense, then fled and joined the young Rebel Alliance. After Admiral Raddus died at Scarif, Ackbar became supreme commander of the Alliance Fleet. He later led the Mon Calamari mutiny that brought the Mercantile Fleet's cruisers over to the rebels, and directed the fleet from Home One at the Battle of Endor. As a fleet admiral of the New Republic he won the decisive Battle of Jakku, then retired to Mon Cala. Decades later Leia Organa talked him out of retirement to help the Resistance. He oversaw the attack on Starkiller Base and was killed on the bridge of the Raddus when First Order fighters attacked the fleeing Resistance fleet.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Gial_Ac.socialDesc: Gial Ackbar, the admiral who led the rebel fleet at Endor and won at Jakku, fought for sixty years and died on the Raddus as the Resistance fled D'Qar.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Gial_Ac.timeline:
~55 BBY - Birth on Mon Cala

Born on Mon Cala in the last years of the Galactic Republic. Canon only places his birth between about 61 and 52 BBY.

Before 20 BBY - Council Seat and Rise in the Guard

Represents Coral City on the Calamari Council, then joins the Mon Calamari Guard and rises to captain, becoming chief military advisor to the throne.

~20 BBY - Battle of Mon Cala

After King Yos Kolina is assassinated, Ackbar protects Prince Lee-Char as Quarren separatists and Riff Tamson's droid forces attack Coral City. He fights beside Anakin Skywalker, Kit Fisto and Ahsoka Tano and is taken prisoner.

~20 BBY - Liberation and Coronation

Leads the prisoners' uprising once Lee-Char wins the Quarren over. Tamson is defeated, and Ackbar stands beside the throne at Lee-Char's coronation.

18 BBY - Imperial Invasion of Mon Cala

As Commander and Chief of Security, he confronts Darth Vader and the Inquisitors, defends the northern hemisphere and destroys an Imperial sky-base. The Empire still takes the planet.

After 18 BBY - Joins the Rebellion

Flees Mon Cala and joins the nascent Alliance to Restore the Republic. At one point he is enslaved by Tarkin until rebels rescue him.

1 BBY - Supreme Commander of the Fleet

After Admiral Raddus dies at Scarif, Ackbar takes command of the Alliance Fleet. He sends ships to protect Alderaanian refugees at Fostar Haven.

0 ABY - Evacuation of Yavin 4

Helps organize the rebel evacuation of the Great Temple after the Battle of Yavin.

0 ABY - Missions with Luke Skywalker

Sends Luke to Rodia, to scout the moon Fex and to extract Drusil Bephorin from Denon. He also backs the plan to hijack the Star Destroyer Harbinger to relieve Tureen VII.

~1 ABY - Mutiny at Mon Cala

Answers King Lee-Char's dying call and leads the Mon Cala Mercantile Fleet in a mutiny against the Empire. Captain Pysk Lila sacrifices the Aurora Flare to open an escape route.

~1 ABY - Assault on Mako-Ta Space Docks

Survives Death Squadron's ambush on the sabotaged new fleet and gets Home One away into hyperspace.

3 ABY - Hoth and the Road to Endor

Keeps the Alliance Fleet together after the Empire's attack on Echo Base.

4 ABY - Battle of Endor

Commands the rebel fleet from Home One, realizes the Imperial trap and holds the line until the second Death Star is destroyed.

4–5 ABY - New Republic Fleet Admiral

Becomes a fleet admiral of the New Republic Defense Fleet and leads the campaign against the Imperial remnants.

5 ABY - Battle of Jakku

Leads the New Republic to its decisive victory over the Empire, then retires to Mon Cala.

~9 ABY - New Republic Council

Appears as a senior New Republic figure during the era of Ahsoka.

34 ABY - Returns to Serve the Resistance

Leia Organa persuades him out of retirement. He takes back his admiral's commission at the D'Qar base and helps oversee the destruction of Starkiller Base.

34 ABY - Death aboard the Raddus

Killed on the Raddus's bridge when Kylo Ren and his TIE escorts attack the fleet during the evacuation of D'Qar.

birth.source: Wookieepedia infobox: 'Between c. 61 BBY and c. 52 BBY, Mon Cala'. No exact year is canon; 55 BBY sits inside that range.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: died 34 ABY aboard the Raddus in the Oetchi system (Star Wars: The Last Jedi).

notes.detail: Ackbar's son Aftab Ackbar appears in The Rise of Skywalker as a Resistance pilot. He could be added as a family link or a character of his own.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Breha_O.description: Breha Organa ruled Alderaan as its queen through the last years of the Republic and the rise of the Empire, and helped found the Rebel Alliance. As a teenager she nearly died during the Challenge of the Body on her Day of Demand. Her heart and lungs were replaced with pulmonodes, and she chose to leave them visible as a reminder that she had survived. Her injuries led her and her husband, Bail, to decide against having biological children. At the end of the Clone Wars they adopted the newborn daughter of Padmé Amidala and Anakin Skywalker, raised her as Princess Leia, and never told her who her birth parents were. Breha was also Alderaan's minister of education. Under the Empire she mentored young Alderaanians in their world's heritage, took in refugees, and used palace banquets as cover for strategy meetings that helped unite scattered resistance cells into the Alliance. She oversaw Leia's Day of Demand and later admitted to her daughter that she and Bail were part of the rebellion. When an Inquisitor had Leia kidnapped to draw out Obi-Wan Kenobi, she lived through the fear of losing her. Breha died in 1 BBY, alongside Bail, when the Death Star destroyed Alderaan, and the galaxy remembered them as martyrs of the rebellion.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Breha_O.socialDesc: Breha Organa, Queen of Alderaan, raised Leia as her own, helped found the Rebel Alliance, and died when the Death Star destroyed her world in 1 BBY.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Breha_O.timeline:
~45 BBY - Birth on Alderaan

Born into the Elder Houses as heir to the Alderaanian throne and raised in the Royal Palace at Aldera. Canon gives no exact year.

~29 BBY - Day of Demand and the Accident

At sixteen she claims the throne through her Day of Demand. A fall during her Challenge of the Body nearly kills her. Her heart and lungs are replaced with pulmonodes, which she leaves visible, and she is invested as crown princess.

Between 40 and 28 BBY - Queen and Marriage

She takes the throne of Alderaan and marries Bail Prestor Organa. Because of her injuries, the couple decide to adopt an heir rather than conceive one.

28 BBY - Hosting Padmé Amidala

She invites Senator Padmé Amidala to Alderaan for a week. The two talk about motherhood, monarchy and Naboo's defenses.

22–19 BBY - Clone Wars Humanitarian Efforts

She sends doctors, teachers, builders and supplies to worlds devastated by the war. Alderaan hosts a conference to help war refugees.

19 BBY - Adoption of Leia

After Padmé's death, Bail brings the infant Leia home, and Breha takes her in as her daughter. Leia is presented as Princess of Alderaan on her Name Day, and her true parentage is kept secret.

~18–10 BBY - Raising the Princess and Mentoring Alderaanians

She raises Leia, tells her stories of Padmé Amidala, and teaches her orchid care, piloting and leadership. She also mentors young Alderaanians such as Evaan Verlaine in their world's heritage.

9 BBY - Leia's Kidnapping

Leia is abducted during a family visit on orders from the Third Sister, who wants to lure out Obi-Wan Kenobi. Breha and Bail ask Kenobi for help. After he rescues Leia, Breha thanks him on Alderaan.

3 BBY - Leia's Day of Demand

She presides over Leia's Day of Demand and gives her the Rhindon Sword. Meanwhile she hosts banquets that double as secret strategy meetings for the growing rebellion.

3 BBY - Refugees from Wobani

She welcomes the refugees Leia brings back from Wobani and gives each of them a stipend. Afterwards she scolds Leia for derailing Bail's relocation negotiations.

~3–2 BBY - Revealing the Rebellion to Leia

Once Leia uncovers her parents' rebel activity, Breha and Bail admit it but keep the details from her to protect her.

2 BBY - Founding of the Rebel Alliance

After Mon Mothma breaks with the Empire, the resistance networks that Breha and Bail helped build are formally united as the Alliance to Restore the Republic.

1 BBY - Death in the Destruction of Alderaan

Days after the Battle of Scarif, the Death Star destroys Alderaan, killing Breha and Bail.

birth.source: Wookieepedia's infobox leaves the birth field blank. The only anchors are that her Day of Demand came at age sixteen and that she became queen and married Bail sometime between 40 and 28 BBY. That puts her birth roughly between 56 and 44 BBY, so our 45 BBY guess is plausible but not canon.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: died 1 BBY on Alderaan, in the destruction of Alderaan by the Death Star (A New Hope).

notes.detail: Canon gives no birth year. Wookieepedia places her ascension and marriage somewhere between 40 and 28 BBY and says her Day of Demand came at age sixteen, so any year from about 56 to 44 BBY fits. Keeping -45 flagged as a guess is appropriate.

Wookieepedia flags a continuity conflict between Queen's Shadow and Master & Apprentice about Breha and Bail's marriage and reign. That conflict is why the article only gives a 40–28 BBY window for her ascension and marriage, so dates for those events should stay vague.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Greedo.description: Greedo is best remembered for the way he died: cornering Han Solo in the Mos Eisley cantina on Jabba the Hutt's behalf, only to be gunned down across the table before he could collect. His life leading up to that moment was a string of bad luck and overconfidence. As a hot-tempered youngster in Mos Espa he picked a fight with Anakin Skywalker, accusing him of cheating in the Boonta Eve Classic. During the Clone Wars he took a Trade Federation contract to kidnap the daughters of Pantora's Chairman Papanoida, but a smear of his own blood led the chairman to him, and Jabba forced Greedo to lead the Pantorans to the hostage. As one of Jabba's mid-level hired guns he ran scams such as freeing bounties so he could recapture them, joined Solo and Chewbacca on a doomed heist for a verillix urn on Corellia, shot Solo during the double-crosses that followed, and later botched a job on Mygeeto that nearly got him fed to a rancor. Sent after Solo as his last chance with the Hutt, he finally had the smuggler at blasterpoint in 1 BBY and gloated long enough to be shot dead. Even then his death earned him more fame than anything he did while alive.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Greedo.socialDesc: Greedo, Jabba the Hutt's Rodian bounty hunter, tried to collect on Han Solo in the Mos Eisley cantina and became more famous for dying than living.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Greedo.timeline:
44 BBY - Birth

Greedo is born a Rodian and later moves to Tatooine as a youth, growing up in Mos Espa.

32 BBY - Scuffle with Anakin Skywalker

After the Boonta Eve Classic, Greedo accuses young Anakin Skywalker of cheating to beat Sebulba and starts a fight. His friend Wald warns him that picking fights will lead to a bad end.

~21 BBY - Kidnapping of the Papanoida Daughters

Now working for Jabba the Hutt, Greedo is hired by the Trade Federation to abduct Chairman Papanoida's daughters to pressure Pantora into joining the Separatists. Che Amanwe strikes him with an idol and leaves his blood on it.

~21 BBY - Exposed at Jabba's Palace

Papanoida and his son Ion trace the blood to Greedo and present the evidence to Jabba. The Hutt forces Greedo to lead them to the Mos Eisley cantina, where the kidnappers are killed in a firefight. Greedo slips away.

Imperial Era - Trouble in Mos Eisley

While Obi-Wan Kenobi is in exile on Tatooine, a blaster-wielding Sullustan confronts Greedo in the back alley behind Chalmun's Cantina.

Imperial Era - Capturing Figrin D'an

Greedo delivers the indebted bandleader Figrin D'an to Jabba. While they serve the Hutt, the Modal Nodes learn that Greedo has been releasing small-time bounties so he can recapture them. They later tell Jabba, and a grudge forms.

Imperial Era - The Urn Heist on Corellia

Jabba pairs Greedo with Han Solo and Chewbacca to steal a verillix urn holding the ashes of Krestrel D'Naran. The break-in at Augustus Graves' penthouse fails, and Solo leaves Greedo stranded on Corellia.

Imperial Era - Betraying Solo

Picked up by Khel Tanna's crew, Greedo helps chase the impostor Corbus Tyra and shoots Solo in the chest on Paqualis III. He then helps recover the Millennium Falcon from an Imperial impound on Iakar and cheats his way to ownership of the ship at sabacc.

Imperial Era - Collecting on a Fake

Solo interrogates Greedo and knocks him out to retake the Falcon. Greedo then teams up with Tyra, passes burnt ronto meat off to Jabba as D'Naran's ashes, and collects the reward.

Imperial Era - Failure on Mygeeto

Sent by Jabba to kill IGBC Vice Chairman Anolo and seize a Givin codebreaker, Greedo kills Anolo and takes Ki-Adi-Mundi's old lightsaber, but loses the codebreaker. Jabba threatens to feed him to a rancor until Dok-Ondar buys the lightsaber.

1 BBY - The Hunt for Han Solo

Jabba gives Greedo one last chance: collect the bounty on Solo for dumping a Hutt cargo. Greedo hires Ponda Baba and Doctor Evazan as backup and leans on the Bith musician Lirin Car'n over a debt.

1 BBY - Death in Chalmun's Cantina

After his backup is lost to Obi-Wan Kenobi's lightsaber, Greedo corners Solo alone and demands the money or the Millennium Falcon. He gloats for too long, and Solo shoots him dead from under the table. Wuher drags his body out of the cantina.

1 BBY - Aftermath

Rodians on Tatooine swear revenge on Solo, but he has already left the planet. Greedo's career is soon forgotten, remembered only for how it ended.

birth.source: Wookieepedia Greedo infobox and Early life section: born 44 BBY (from canon reference material such as Ultimate Star Wars and the Databank-era references).

death.source: Wookieepedia Greedo infobox: died 1 BBY on Tatooine, shot by Han Solo in Chalmun's Cantina during A New Hope (dated 1 BBY under the Galactic Atlas convention).

notes.detail: The Wookieepedia infobox lists both Rodia and Tatooine as homeworlds. Greedo came from Rodia but grew up in Mos Espa and lived his whole adult life on Tatooine.
His employment by Jabba the Hutt drives nearly all of his canon story, including the bounty on Solo.

notes.current: The Clone Wars (TV series); Episode IV: A New Hope
notes.detail: Greedo also appears in a deleted scene of Episode I: The Phantom Menace (his fight with Anakin), which Wookieepedia lists as a canon appearance marked 'deleted'. Leaving it out of seenIn is defensible because the scene is not in the theatrical cut.

Canon sources disagree. 'The Luckless Rodian' (From a Certain Point of View) says Greedo had never seen a lightsaber in person, but Galaxy's Edge 2 shows him stealing Ki-Adi-Mundi's lightsaber on Mygeeto. Wookieepedia follows the newer comic. The exact years of his Imperial-era jobs (the urn heist from the Han Solo & Chewbacca comic, the Mygeeto job) are not given in the article, so they are listed without years.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dooku.description: Dooku was one of the finest duelists the Jedi Order ever produced. He spent most of his long life as a Jedi, then gave it up and became Darth Tyranus, the Sith apprentice who led the galaxy into the Clone Wars. His father, the Count of Serenno, abandoned him as a baby, and Jedi seekers took him in. He grew up in the Temple as Yoda's Padawan, and his curiosity about the dark side worried his teachers even then. As a Jedi Master he trained Rael Averross and Qui-Gon Jinn and later sat on the High Council. Over the decades, a corrupt Senate and a Council he saw as too cautious wore down his faith. In 42 BBY he left the Order, overthrew his brother Ramil and took back the title of Count. Qui-Gon's death at Naboo pushed him further, and after he killed Master Yaddle he became Darth Sidious's apprentice. He then helped set up the secret clone army and gathered thousands of star systems into the Confederacy of Independent Systems. As the Separatists' Head of State he opened the war at Geonosis in 22 BBY. He trained General Grievous and Asajj Ventress, betrayed Ventress on his master's orders, and later tried to groom Savage Opress and Quinlan Vos to replace her. In 19 BBY he took Chancellor Palpatine hostage during the Battle of Coruscant. There Anakin Skywalker beat him in a duel aboard the Invisible Hand and executed him at Palpatine's urging. Dooku never learned that he had only ever been a placeholder until Sidious found a new apprentice.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dooku.socialDesc: Count Dooku, Yoda's Padawan turned Sith Lord Darth Tyranus, led the Separatists into the Clone Wars before Anakin Skywalker beheaded him above Coruscant.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dooku.timeline:
102 BBY - Birth on Serenno

Born to Count Gora and Countess Anya of House Serenno. His Force powers show early, and his frightened father leaves the baby outside the palace. A Jedi seeker rescues him and brings him to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant.

~101 BBY - Youngling of the Hawk-Bat Clan

Raised in the Temple under Master Tera Sinube, alongside his close friend Sifo-Dyas and his rival Arath Tarrex.

90 BBY - Return to Serenno

At 12, visits Serenno for a galactic festival with Yoda. He saves his siblings Jenza and Ramil from kidnappers, is trapped with Jenza when a building collapses, and learns that Count Gora is his father. He keeps in touch with Jenza for years afterward.

88 BBY - Break-in at the Bogan Collection

Sneaks into the Temple's vault of dark side artifacts with Sifo-Dyas and accidentally hurts his friend through the Force. The incident leads to a duel with Lene Kostana, who later becomes a mentor to him.

86 BBY - Padawan of Yoda

Passes the Initiate Trials at 16. He beats Sifo-Dyas in the Padawan tournament, but Kostana picks Sifo-Dyas, and Grand Master Yoda takes Dooku as his apprentice instead.

~85 BBY - Protobranch Disaster

Defies the Council to warn the Republic about Sifo-Dyas's vision of a solar storm. The storm kills much of Protobranch's population, and Dooku's trust in the Council and the Senate is badly shaken.

~82 BBY - Mother's Funeral and Asusto

His father attacks him at Countess Anya's funeral. Soon afterward, cultists capture him on Asusto, where he sees visions of his future and uses Force lightning for the first time.

~80 BBY - Knight, Master and Teacher

Finishes his training and rises to Jedi Master, becoming known as one of the best lightsaber duelists of his generation. He takes Rael Averross as his first Padawan and trains him for about ten years.

68 BBY - Takes Qui-Gon Jinn as Padawan

At 34, chooses 12-year-old Qui-Gon Jinn as his apprentice. On Numidian Prime he saves Qui-Gon from the bounty hunter Shenda Mol with Force lightning.

~64–60 BBY - Senator Dagonet's Son

While helping recover a senator's kidnapped son, he watches the senator's troops massacre villagers. In his anger he reaches for the dark side and nearly chokes the senator to death before Qui-Gon stops him.

~58 BBY - Joins the Jedi High Council

Uncovers Master Yula Braylon as a leak on the Council after Ramil's airspeeder is sabotaged at the Dragonfire Air Rally. He accepts a Council seat, and Qui-Gon is knighted around the same time.

~50–48 BBY - Investigation on Raxus Secundus

With Mace Windu, looks into Master Katri's murder and finds corruption in the Senate. Windu is given the Council seat Dooku hoped for, which leaves Dooku resentful.

42 BBY - Leaves the Jedi Order

Becomes one of the Lost Twenty, returns to Serenno, overthrows his corrupt brother Ramil and takes the title of Count. He begins talking in secret with Darth Sidious.

32 BBY - Death of Qui-Gon and Fall to the Dark Side

Qui-Gon Jinn is killed at the Battle of Naboo. Dooku then kills Master Yaddle in a duel in the Works and becomes Sidious's apprentice under the name Darth Tyranus.

~32 BBY - Seizing the Clone Army

Has Sifo-Dyas killed, takes over the clone army Sifo-Dyas had ordered on Kamino, and recruits Jango Fett as the clones' template. Around the same time he kills his sister Jenza to prove his loyalty to Sidious.

~32–22 BBY - Architect of the Separatist Crisis

Uses his wealth and charm to draw thousands of star systems into a secessionist movement while the droid army is built up in secret.

22 BBY - First Battle of Geonosis

As Head of State of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, sees the Clone Wars break out. He cuts off Anakin Skywalker's arm, duels Yoda and escapes with the Death Star plans.

22–20 BBY - Master of the Separatist War

Commands the war through General Grievous and his dark apprentice Asajj Ventress. He is captured more than once, including by the pirate Hondo Ohnaka, and each time gets away.

~20 BBY - Betrayal of Ventress

On Sidious's orders, tries to have Ventress killed. He then survives a Nightsister plot against him involving Savage Opress, and he and Grievous later attack Dathomir.

19 BBY - The Quinlan Vos Affair

Takes the Jedi Quinlan Vos as a secret apprentice. Vos turns out to be loyal to the Jedi after all, and Dooku narrowly escapes.

19 BBY - Death at the Battle of Coruscant

Helps take Chancellor Palpatine hostage. Aboard the Invisible Hand, Anakin Skywalker defeats him and beheads him at Palpatine's urging.

birth.source: Wookieepedia 'Dooku' infobox (born 102 BBY, Serenno) and biography; consistent with stated ages (12 in 90 BBY, 34 in 68 BBY).

death.source: Wookieepedia 'Dooku' infobox (died 19 BBY, Invisible Hand, Coruscant system); Episode III: Revenge of the Sith.

notes.current: Episode II: Attack of the Clones; The Clone Wars (movie); The Clone Wars (TV series); Episode III: Revenge of the Sith
notes.detail: Tales of the Jedi (2022) centers several episodes on Dooku ('Justice', 'Choices', 'The Sith Lord'). They cover his years as a Jedi Master, his killing of Yaddle and his turn to become Tyranus. All are cited in the Wookieepedia article.

notes.suggested: Add Affiliation: Jedi Order / Sith / Confederacy of Independent Systems, and Masters: Yoda, Darth Sidious
notes.detail: His two masters and his switch from Jedi to Separatist leader are central to the character, but our entry doesn't record them.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Anakin_.description: The prophesied Chosen One who was meant to bring balance to the Force, Anakin Skywalker went from enslaved boy to celebrated Jedi hero, then became the Sith Lord Darth Vader, and was finally redeemed by his son. Born a slave to Shmi Skywalker with no father, he had an unmatched midi-chlorian count. Qui-Gon Jinn found him at age nine, and he won his freedom in the Boonta Eve podrace. Later that year he destroyed the Trade Federation's droid control ship at the Battle of Naboo. The Jedi Council had doubts about him, but he trained under Obi-Wan Kenobi and secretly married Padmé Amidala at the start of the Clone Wars. During the war he earned the name "Hero With No Fear" commanding the 501st Legion, and he trained Ahsoka Tano as his Padawan. Palpatine played on his fear of losing Padmé, and in 19 BBY he turned to the dark side, led the attack on the Jedi Temple during Order 66, and was left maimed after his duel with Kenobi on Mustafar. Rebuilt as an armored cyborg, Vader spent two decades hunting Jedi and enforcing the Emperor's rule. He killed Kenobi aboard the Death Star, discovered that Luke was his son, and tried to turn him. At the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY, seeing Luke tortured brought Anakin back. He threw Palpatine to his death, fulfilled the prophecy at the cost of his own life, and became one with the Force.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Anakin_.socialDesc: Anakin Skywalker rose from Tatooine slave to Jedi hero of the Clone Wars, fell as Darth Vader, and was redeemed at Endor by destroying the Emperor.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Anakin_.timeline:
41 BBY - Birth

Born to the slave Shmi Skywalker, who conceived him without a father. Sources disagree on whether he was born on Tatooine or brought there as an infant.

~38 BBY - Sold to Watto

At about age three, Gardulla the Hutt loses Anakin and his mother to the Toydarian junk dealer Watto in a podracing bet.

~33 BBY - Builds C-3PO and a Podracer

While working in Watto's shop in Mos Espa, he builds the protocol droid C-3PO from scrap to help his mother and assembles his own podracer.

32 BBY - Discovered by Qui-Gon Jinn

Meets Qui-Gon Jinn and Padmé Amidala, who is disguised as a handmaiden. A blood test shows a midi-chlorian count higher than Yoda's.

32 BBY - Wins the Boonta Eve Classic

Wins the podrace, which pays for the Queen's ship repairs and earns him his freedom. He leaves his mother behind to go with the Jedi.

32 BBY - Tested by the Jedi Council

The Council judges him too old and too fearful to be trained, but lets him go with Qui-Gon to Naboo.

32 BBY - Battle of Naboo

Flying an N-1 starfighter, he destroys the Trade Federation's droid control ship. Qui-Gon dies, and Obi-Wan Kenobi takes Anakin as his Padawan.

22 BBY - Guardian of Padmé

Assigned to protect Senator Amidala after attempts on her life, he goes into hiding with her on Naboo and falls in love with her.

22 BBY - Death of Shmi and the Tusken Massacre

Troubled by visions, he returns to Tatooine and finds his mother dying in a Tusken Raider camp. In his rage he slaughters the entire tribe.

22 BBY - First Battle of Geonosis

Loses his right arm fighting Count Dooku as the Clone Wars begin, and is fitted with a cybernetic replacement.

22 BBY - Secret Wedding

Marries Padmé Amidala in secret on Naboo, breaking the Jedi Code.

22 BBY - Knighthood and Ahsoka Tano

Now a Jedi Knight and General of the 501st Legion, he is given Ahsoka Tano as his Padawan during the Battle of Christophsis and the rescue of Jabba's son.

~21 BBY - Mortis

On Mortis, the Father tests him as the Chosen One. He glimpses his future as Darth Vader, but the memory is erased.

19 BBY - Ahsoka Leaves the Order

Ahsoka is falsely accused of bombing the Jedi Temple. Even after she is cleared, she walks away from the Order, and Anakin's faith in the Jedi is badly shaken.

19 BBY - Battle of Coruscant

Rescues Chancellor Palpatine and executes Count Dooku at Palpatine's urging. He is then seated on the Jedi Council but denied the rank of Master.

19 BBY - Becomes Darth Vader

Learns that Palpatine is Darth Sidious and helps him strike down Mace Windu, hoping Sidious can save Padmé from the deaths he has foreseen. He pledges himself to the Sith as Darth Vader.

19 BBY - Order 66

Leads the 501st in the attack on the Jedi Temple and kills its inhabitants, younglings included. He then wipes out the Separatist Council on Mustafar.

19 BBY - Duel on Mustafar

Chokes Padmé in a fit of rage and loses a duel to Obi-Wan, who leaves him maimed and burning. Palpatine has him rebuilt in a life-support suit. Padmé dies after giving birth to Luke and Leia.

~18 BBY - Jedi Hunter

As the Emperor's enforcer, he hunts down surviving Jedi and oversees the Inquisitorius.

9 BBY - Hunting Kenobi

Draws Obi-Wan out of hiding and fights him twice. In their second duel Kenobi damages his helmet and leaves him behind.

2 BBY - Confronts the Ghost Crew

Moves against the growing rebel movement at Lothal and in the Siege of Lothal. Ahsoka Tano learns that her former master has become Vader.

2 BBY - Duel on Malachor

Duels Ahsoka inside the Sith temple on Malachor and nearly dies in its collapse.

1 BBY - Battle of Scarif

Boards the rebel flagship Profundity and slaughters its crew, but fails to recover the stolen Death Star plans.

1 BBY - Kills Obi-Wan Kenobi

Captures Princess Leia, his own daughter though neither knows it, and strikes down Kenobi aboard the Death Star.

0 BBY - Battle of Yavin

Survives the Death Star's destruction and learns that the pilot who destroyed it was a Skywalker, his son.

3 ABY - Battle of Hoth and Cloud City

Leads the attack on Echo Base and pursues Luke to Bespin. There he cuts off Luke's hand, reveals that he is Luke's father, and offers to rule the galaxy with him.

4 ABY - Redemption and Death at Endor

Brings Luke before the Emperor aboard the second Death Star. Watching Sidious torture his son, he turns on his master and throws him down a reactor shaft, taking mortal wounds from the lightning. He dies unmasked beside Luke and becomes one with the Force.

4 ABY - Appears as a Force Spirit

Appears as a Force spirit on Endor alongside Obi-Wan and Yoda during the victory celebration.

~9 ABY - Teaches Ahsoka in the World Between Worlds

Appears to Ahsoka Tano in the World Between Worlds for a last lesson, making her face the choice between life and death.

35 ABY - Voice at Exegol

He is one of the Jedi voices that urge Rey to bring back the balance during the Battle of Exegol.

birth.source: Wookieepedia infobox: 41 BBY. The 'disputed' tag refers to his birthplace (Tatooine vs. being brought there as an infant), not the year. The 32 BBY events of The Phantom Menace, when he is 9, match it.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: died 4 ABY aboard the second Death Star in the Endor system during the Battle of Endor (Return of the Jedi).

notes.detail: Anakin appears on screen in the Ahsoka episodes of Tales of the Jedi (2022), including her Padawan training and Order 66.

notes.suggested: Episode IX: The Rise of Skywalker
notes.detail: Hayden Christensen's voice is among the Jedi voices speaking to Rey on Exegol. It is a voice-only appearance, so include it only if seenIn counts voice cameos.

Wookieepedia marks his birthplace as disputed: some records say Tatooine, others say he was brought there very young. Tatooine is still correct as his homeworld. The birth year, 41 BBY, is not in dispute.

seenIn includes Ahsoka (~9 ABY), where he appears after death in the World Between Worlds, while the column ends in 4 ABY. That is correct for a death year, but the app should present post-death appearances as a Force spirit, not as a living character.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Grievou.description: General Grievous was the Confederacy's most feared battlefield commander during the Clone Wars. He was a four-armed cyborg who hunted Jedi and kept their lightsabers as trophies. Born Qymaen jai Sheelal, he was a sniper by the age of eight. He rose to become a legendary warlord of the Kaleesh and took the name Grievous during his people's brutal war against the Yam'rii of Huk. When the Republic and the Jedi stepped in on the Yam'rii side, the sanctions that followed starved his people, and he swore revenge. He went on to serve the InterGalactic Banking Clan as an enforcer and slowly traded his body for machine parts. Then a shuttle crash, secretly arranged by Count Dooku, left him barely alive, and Separatist surgeons rebuilt him almost entirely. Only his brain, eyes, spinal cord and a few vital organs survived. Dooku trained him in lightsaber combat, and he became Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies. Across the war he led countless campaigns, killed many Jedi and fought repeated duels with his nemesis, Obi-Wan Kenobi. In the war's final days in 19 BBY he led the attack on Coruscant and captured Chancellor Palpatine. After Dooku's death he became acting leader of the Separatists and fled to Utapau. There Kenobi tracked him down and killed him, and the Confederacy soon collapsed.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Grievou.socialDesc: General Grievous, the cyborg Kaleesh warlord who led the Separatist droid armies, hunted Jedi for their lightsabers, and was slain by Obi-Wan on Utapau.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Grievou.timeline:
Before the Clone Wars - Birth on Kalee

Qymaen jai Sheelal is born in the wilds of Kalee while the Kaleesh are fighting a war against the insectoid Yam'rii of Huk.

Before the Clone Wars - Child sniper

His father teaches him to shoot an Outland rifle. By the age of eight he is serving as a sniper and has already killed forty enemies.

Before the Clone Wars - Warlord "Grievous"

He rises quickly to become a feared warlord and takes the name Grievous. He gathers Kalee's elite Izvoshra warriors as his personal bodyguard.

Before the Clone Wars - Campaigns against Huk

Grievous drives the Yam'rii off Kalee and takes the war to the Huk worlds. His successes catch the attention of Dooku and Darth Sidious.

Before the Clone Wars - Republic intervention

The Republic and the Jedi take the Yam'rii side. The sanctions that follow starve hundreds of thousands of Kaleesh, and Grievous swears vengeance.

Before the Clone Wars - Enforcer for the Banking Clan

Grievous becomes an enforcer for the InterGalactic Banking Clan and commands its droid army. He is forbidden to keep the Izvoshra, so he has the IG-100 MagnaGuards built and trains them himself.

Before the Clone Wars - Cybernetic transformation

With the Sith's encouragement, Grievous begins replacing parts of his body with cybernetic upgrades.

Before the Clone Wars - Shuttle crash and rebuilding

Dooku secretly sabotages his shuttle and blames the Jedi for the crash. Separatist and Geonosian surgeons rebuild the dying warlord as an almost entirely mechanical four-armed cyborg and alter his mind without his knowledge.

Before the Clone Wars - Lightsaber training

Dooku trains Grievous in lightsaber combat and gives him his first captured Jedi lightsaber. Grievous passes his skills on to his MagnaGuards.

22 BBY - First Battle of Geonosis

Grievous fights in secret in the Geonosian catacombs. He kills the Jedi who stumble on him so that the Separatist Council can escape, and none survive to report his existence.

22 BBY - Supreme Martial Commander

He is made a general and Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies, second only to Dooku. Early in the war he scars Ki-Adi-Mundi.

~22 BBY - The Malevolence campaign

His flagship, the Malevolence, wipes out Republic fleets with its ion cannon until Anakin Skywalker's forces destroy it.

~22 BBY - Vassek 3

At his fortress on Vassek 3, Grievous fights Kit Fisto and kills Fisto's former Padawan, Nahdar Vebb.

~22 BBY - Hunting Jedi

Grievous captures Jedi Master Eeth Koth to lure Kenobi into a trap. The Republic rescues Koth, and Grievous escapes.

~21 BBY - Captured by pirates

Hondo Ohnaka's pirates briefly hold Grievous prisoner. Kenobi and Anakin nearly capture him before he gets away.

~20 BBY - Assault on Dathomir

On Dooku's orders, Grievous leads a droid army that massacres the Nightsisters of Dathomir.

~20 BBY - Return to Kalee

On his homeworld, Grievous clashes with Anakin Skywalker during a mission to recover the kidnapped Jedi A'Sharad Hett.

19 BBY - Clash with Maul and Mother Talzin

Grievous leads Separatist forces against Maul's Shadow Collective. Dooku and Grievous kill Mother Talzin.

19 BBY - Battle of Coruscant

Grievous leads the raid on the Republic capital and captures Chancellor Palpatine. Kenobi and Skywalker rescue him from the Invisible Hand, Dooku is killed, and Grievous escapes in a pod.

19 BBY - Leader of the Confederacy

As acting head of the Separatists, Grievous retreats to Utapau. On Sidious's orders he sends the Separatist Council to Mustafar.

19 BBY - Death on Utapau

Kenobi confronts him, cuts off two of his arms and chases him across the sinkhole city. He kills Grievous by firing a blaster into his organic gut-sack, and the Clone Wars end soon after.

birth.source: The Wookieepedia infobox leaves the birth field empty. The article only says he was born years before the Clone Wars. The 65 BBY in our data is an unsourced guess, and it is correctly flagged as one.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: died 19 BBY on Utapau, killed by Obi-Wan Kenobi in Episode III: Revenge of the Sith.

notes.detail: No canon source gives Grievous a birth year or age. The only age anchor is that he was a sniper at eight during the Kaleesh-Yam'rii war. Keep startYearUnknown true. Any year we pick is purely a position for drawing the column.
Being almost entirely cybernetic is Grievous's defining trait: only his brain, eyes, spinal cord and a few organs are left. It may be worth recording as a displayed fact if the app supports it.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Nute_Gu.description: Nute Gunray is best remembered as the Trade Federation viceroy who blockaded and invaded Naboo, and whose greed made him a willing tool of Darth Sidious. He had already become viceroy when the Eriadu Conference emptied out the Federation's leadership, and with Sidious secretly behind him he took full control of the conglomerate. In 32 BBY he carried out the Sith Lord's plan: he blockaded Naboo, tried to kill the Jedi envoys Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi, and occupied the planet to force Queen Amidala to sign a treaty. The crisis ended when Amidala captured him in her own throne room. He then went through four Supreme Court trials without being convicted, kept his wealth and his titles, and came out of it with a lasting grudge against Amidala. He put the Federation's droid armies behind Count Dooku's Separatists in exchange for her assassination, which failed. From Geonosis he watched the Clone Wars begin. During the war he schemed against Amidala on Rodia, was captured by the Republic, and escaped with Asajj Ventress's help. When Dooku and Grievous were dead, he fled with the Separatist Council to Mustafar expecting the peace Sidious had promised. Instead Darth Vader killed the whole council, and Gunray was the last to die, begging for his life. Imperial records later claimed he had taken his own life.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Nute_Gu.socialDesc: Nute Gunray led the Trade Federation's blockade of Naboo, survived four trials, and bankrolled the Separatists until Darth Vader cut him down on Mustafar.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Nute_Gu.timeline:
34 BBY - Viceroy of the Trade Federation

Gunray has become Viceroy of the Trade Federation, with Darth Sidious quietly steering his rise.

33 BBY - Seizing control after Eriadu

The disastrous Eriadu Conference leaves a power vacuum at the top of the Federation. Gunray takes total control of the conglomerate, and Lott Dod takes its Senate seat.

32 BBY - Blockade of Naboo

After a trade-route taxation dispute, Gunray's fleet blockades Naboo from his flagship, the Saak'ak. On Sidious's orders he tries to kill the Jedi envoys Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi.

32 BBY - Occupation of Naboo

His droid army takes Theed and forces the population into camps. Gunray sits on Amidala's throne, holds Governor Sio Bibble prisoner, and keeps demanding that the queen sign his treaty.

32 BBY - Captured at the Battle of Naboo

Amidala tricks his droids with a decoy and takes Gunray and Rune Haako prisoner in the throne room. When the Droid Control Ship is destroyed, his army shuts down, and he is sent to Coruscant for trial.

32 BBY–28 BBY - Four Supreme Court trials

For four years expensive lawyers keep him out of trouble. The third trial ends in a hung jury and the fourth finds him not guilty, so he keeps his assets and titles. He blames Amidala and has the Federation spread rumors against her through the press.

24 BBY - Joining the Separatist movement

After Dooku's Raxus Address, Gunray allies with the new Confederacy of Independent Systems. His condition is that Senator Amidala be killed.

22 BBY - Plot against Amidala

Dooku hires Jango Fett and Zam Wesell to kill Amidala, and both attempts fail. On Geonosis, Gunray refuses to sign the Separatist treaty until he has her head on his desk.

22 BBY - First Battle of Geonosis

He watches the execution arena and the Jedi rescue, then flees as the clone army arrives. The Federation core ships are evacuated as the Clone Wars break out.

22 BBY - Mission on Nooroyo

Early in the war, Gunray goes to Nooroyo in person to negotiate a spice deal. Amidala and Anakin Skywalker are on the planet at the same time and have to leave in a hurry.

22 BBY - Trap on Rodia

He promises relief supplies to Rodia in return for Senator Onaconda Farr handing over Amidala. The plan backfires, and Gunray is captured by Republic forces.

22 BBY - Escape from the Tranquility

While he is being taken to Coruscant, the traitorous Senate Guard captain Faro Argyus and Asajj Ventress free him. He flees with Ventress, who then kills Argyus.

22 BBY - Bait on Vassek

A hologram of Gunray lures Kit Fisto and Nahdar Vebb into General Grievous's fortress, where Grievous is waiting for them.

~21 BBY - Lending the fleet to Cad Bane

On Sidious's orders, Gunray sends Federation warships to support Cad Bane at Devaron. He is furious when Bane loses ship after ship to the Republic.

19 BBY - Council on Utapau

After Dooku's death, Gunray openly challenges Grievous's ability to protect the Separatist Council. The council is then sent to Mustafar just before the Republic attacks Utapau.

19 BBY - Death on Mustafar

Sidious sends Darth Vader, supposedly to make peace. Vader kills the entire Separatist Council, and Gunray is the last to die, begging for his life. The Empire later records his death as a suicide and dissolves the Trade Federation.

~3 ABY - Remains found by Vader

Sidious leaves Vader stranded on Mustafar as punishment. There Vader finds Gunray's decaying body in the ruined Separatist complex and relives the massacre.

Check the film's Wookieepedia appearances list before keeping this entry.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Qui-Gon.description: Qui-Gon Jinn is best known as the Jedi who found Anakin Skywalker, the boy he believed was the Chosen One, and as the mentor whose death set Obi-Wan Kenobi's path. He was a maverick Jedi Master who followed the Living Force even when that meant defying the High Council. He grew up in the Jedi Temple and became Count Dooku's Padawan at twelve. He was knighted around 58 BBY, and in 44 BBY he took Kenobi as his own apprentice. Together they spent a year protecting Duchess Satine Kryze on Mandalore and uncovered a royal plot on Pijal. After Pijal he turned down a seat on the Jedi Council so he could keep training Kenobi. Qui-Gon also learned in secret how to keep his consciousness after death. In 32 BBY he was sent to end the Trade Federation's blockade of Naboo and rescued Queen Amidala. On Tatooine he met the enslaved boy Anakin, whose midi-chlorian count was higher than any on record, and fought off Darth Maul, which proved to him that the Sith had returned. The Council refused to train Anakin. Qui-Gon then went back to Naboo, where Maul mortally wounded him during the battle for Theed. With his last breath he made Kenobi promise to train the boy. Even in death he stayed part of the story: he returned as a voice and then as a Force spirit to guide Yoda and, years later, Kenobi.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Qui-Gon.socialDesc: Qui-Gon Jinn, maverick Jedi Master and Dooku's former Padawan, discovered Anakin Skywalker on Tatooine and fell to Darth Maul in the Battle of Naboo.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Qui-Gon.timeline:
~80 BBY - Birth on Coruscant

Qui-Gon Jinn is born on the galactic capital and later taken to the Jedi Temple, where he joins the Heliost Clan and learns lightsaber combat from Tera Sinube.

~68 BBY - Padawan of Dooku

At twelve he becomes Master Dooku's apprentice. He first sees the holocron of Jedi prophecies, which will fascinate him for the rest of his life.

~68 BBY - First battle on Shurrupak

Four months into his apprenticeship he goes into battle for the first time and meets Rael Averross, Dooku's former Padawan, who becomes a lifelong friend.

Hunting Shenda Mol

On a strike team to Numidian Prime, Qui-Gon is captured by the bounty hunter Shenda Mol. Dooku saves him with Force lightning, which troubles the young Padawan.

~64–60 BBY - Rescue of Senator Dagonet's son

Qui-Gon calms a deadly standoff in which Dooku nearly kills a corrupt senator, and Dooku praises him as the wiser man.

60 BBY - Trials on Felucia

During his trials he falls in love and has a relationship that tests his commitment to the Code. He stays in the Order but keeps a Mustafar fire diamond as a memento.

~58 BBY - Dragonfire Air Rally and knighthood

He and Dooku expose a spy on the Council. Dooku takes a Council seat, and Qui-Gon is made a Jedi Knight around the same time.

44 BBY - Takes Obi-Wan Kenobi as Padawan

At thirty-six, Qui-Gon takes on Obi-Wan Kenobi as his apprentice.

42 BBY - Dooku leaves the Order

His former master's departure shakes him deeply, but he regains his resolve.

~41–40 BBY - Protecting Satine Kryze

He and Kenobi spend a year on the run on Mandalore protecting Duchess Satine Kryze from bounty hunters until the civil war ends.

~41 BBY - Life Day on Kashyyyk

Visiting his Wookiee friend Brennonn, Qui-Gon is captured by Trandoshan hunters. Kenobi rescues him.

40 BBY - Missions to Teth and Pijal

After a mission against Wanbo the Hutt, he is offered a seat on the Jedi Council. On Pijal he uncovers Princess Fanry's plot and saves Czerka's slaves, then turns down the Council seat so he can keep training Kenobi.

~40 BBY - Escorting Lo for Yoda

He and Kenobi help Yoda after a raid on the Flesh Mongers and take the Force-sensitive child Lo to the Temple.

Secrets of eternal life

Taught by the Force Priestesses and a Shaman of the Whills, he secretly begins learning how to keep his consciousness after death.

37 BBY - Crisis of purpose on Bri'n

Called a warrior by Priestess Th'er, he goes looking for answers. A dark Force vision teaches him that balance must come without unchecked violence.

34 BBY - Mission to Oosalon

With Mace Windu, Plo Koon and Depa Billaba, he helps defeat the warlord Guattako, who had kidnapped children to fight for him.

32 BBY - Blockade and invasion of Naboo

He is sent to negotiate with the Trade Federation, survives their attempt to kill him, and rescues Queen Amidala from occupied Theed.

32 BBY - Discovery of Anakin Skywalker

Stranded on Tatooine, he meets young Anakin, wins his freedom in the Boonta Eve race, and fights Darth Maul briefly.

32 BBY - Before the Jedi Council

He insists that Anakin is the Chosen One. The Council refuses to train the boy.

32 BBY - Death on Naboo

In the Battle of Naboo, Darth Maul mortally wounds him. Dying, he makes Kenobi promise to train Anakin and becomes one with the Force.

19 BBY - Voice guiding Yoda

As a disembodied voice, he leads Yoda on a quest to learn how to become a Force spirit.

9 BBY - Appears to Kenobi

After Kenobi's confrontation with Darth Vader, Qui-Gon finally appears to his old apprentice as a Force spirit.

birth.source: Wookieepedia infobox: 'c. 80 BBY, Coruscant'. Other ages in the article agree: 36 years old in 44 BBY and 40 in 40 BBY (Master & Apprentice). The year is given as circa.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: '32 BBY, Naboo'. Killed by Darth Maul during the Battle of Naboo in The Phantom Menace.

notes.detail: The only source for the birth year is 'c. 80 BBY', worked out from his ages in Master & Apprentice. The Wookieepedia article also carries a {{Conflicting}} tag between Master & Apprentice and the Star Wars Character Encyclopedia, New Edition, so a reference book may give a different age. -80 is the best canon value, but it is approximate. It would be good to show it as circa rather than exact.

notes.suggested: Add Obi-Wan Kenobi, Tales of the Jedi and The Clone Wars
notes.detail: He appears as a Force spirit in Obi-Wan Kenobi Part VI. He appears in Tales of the Jedi in 'Justice' and 'The Sith Lord'. In The Clone Wars he appears in the Mortis arc and speaks to Yoda in 'Voices'. He is also heard (voice only) in Attack of the Clones and The Rise of Skywalker.
The infobox lists Dooku as his master and Obi-Wan Kenobi as his apprentice. It also lists Anakin Skywalker as an informal apprentice and Yoda as one he taught as a Force spirit.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Grogu.description: Grogu is the small, Force-gifted foundling whose rescue turned a hardened bounty hunter into a father. As a youngling he was raised at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant and taught by several Masters. When Order 66 struck, Kelleran Beq carried him out of the burning Temple, and for decades afterward he survived by hiding his powers from the Empire. His species ages slowly, so he was about fifty but still looked like an infant when Moff Gideon's Imperial remnant hired Din Djarin to bring him in. Djarin handed him over, then changed his mind and took him back, and the Mandalorian covert on Nevarro declared the pair a clan of two. On their travels Grogu lifted a mudhorn, healed Greef Karga and turned a flamethrower's fire back on an Imperial trooper. On Tython he called out through the Force, was captured by Gideon, and was freed when Luke Skywalker arrived to take him for Jedi training. At Luke's academy he was offered a choice between Yoda's lightsaber and Mandalorian chain mail, and he chose Djarin. He helped retake Mandalore, was formally adopted as Din Grogu, and began training as a Mandalorian. He later worked with his father as a New Republic ally, hunting Imperial warlords and rescuing Rotta the Hutt.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Grogu.socialDesc: Grogu escaped the fall of the Jedi Temple, was rescued by Din Djarin, and turned down Luke Skywalker's training to become a Mandalorian apprentice.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Grogu.timeline:
~41 BBY - Birth

Grogu is born to Yoda's species during the Republic Era. He is later raised at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant as a youngling.

~41 BBY-19 BBY - Youngling at the Jedi Temple

Several Jedi Masters train him over the years. During this time he meets a group of dust bunnies, who give him a flower.

19 BBY - Escape from Order 66

During the attack on the Jedi Temple, Jedi defenders die getting him to safety. Kelleran Beq then flees with him by BARC speeder and escapes Coruscant aboard a Naboo yacht.

19 BBY-9 ABY - Hidden through the Imperial Era

Grogu goes into hiding and conceals his Force abilities, which keeps him from being detected by the Inquisitors. His memories of this period are dark and lonely.

9 ABY - Found on Arvala-7

Din Djarin and IG-11 storm a Nikto camp to claim the bounty on him. Djarin shoots IG-11 before the droid can kill him.

9 ABY - The Mudhorn

Grogu uses the Force to lift a charging mudhorn, which lets Djarin kill it. The effort leaves him unconscious.

9 ABY - Rescued on Nevarro

Djarin delivers Grogu to the Client and Dr. Pershing, then changes his mind and breaks him out. The Mandalorian covert helps them fight off the Bounty Hunters' Guild.

9 ABY - Sorgan and Tatooine

Grogu hides out with Djarin in a krill-farming village on Sorgan. On Tatooine, Peli Motto looks after him, and Toro Calican briefly takes him hostage.

9 ABY - Prison ship job

He rides along on Ranzar Malk's mercenary mission, and Q9-0 nearly kills him before Djarin destroys the droid.

9 ABY - Battle for Nevarro

Grogu heals Greef Karga's wounds and turns an incinerator trooper's flames back on him. The Armorer declares him Djarin's foundling, forming Clan Mudhorn.

9 ABY - Searching for the Jedi

He travels with Djarin to Mos Pelgo, Trask and Nevarro. On Corvus, Ahsoka Tano learns his name and past through the Force but declines to train him.

9 ABY - Captured on Tython

Grogu reaches out through the Force from the seeing stone on Tython. Dark troopers seize him for Moff Gideon.

9 ABY - Rescue by Luke Skywalker

Djarin rescues him from Gideon's cruiser. Luke Skywalker arrives, destroys the dark troopers and takes Grogu away for Jedi training.

9 ABY - Training under Luke

He trains at Luke's new academy site on Ossus. When he has to choose between Yoda's lightsaber and Djarin's gift of beskar chain mail, he chooses the mail.

9 ABY - Return to Din Djarin

Grogu reunites with Djarin on Tatooine during Boba Fett's war against the Pyke Syndicate. He uses the Force to calm a rampaging rancor.

~9 ABY - Liberation of Mandalore

Grogu fights alongside the reunited Mandalorians to defeat Moff Gideon and retake Mandalore. Afterward the Armorer formally makes him Din Grogu, Djarin's son and Mandalorian apprentice.

After 9 ABY - Hunting Imperials for the New Republic

Grogu helps Djarin hunt the warlord Barro, rescues Rotta the Hutt and saves his poisoned father with an antidote. The adventure ends in the destruction of the Hutt Palace on Nal Hutta.

birth.source: Wookieepedia's Grogu infobox gives 'c. 41 BBY'. That date is worked back from The Mandalorian 'Chapter 1', where he is said to be 50 years old in 9 ABY. No source gives an exact birth year.

death.source: Grogu is alive in every canon appearance up to and including The Mandalorian and Grogu.

notes.suggested: true, or label the year as approximate (c. 41 BBY)
notes.detail: Wookieepedia only gives 'c. 41 BBY', worked back from a stated age of 50 in 9 ABY. 41 BBY is the right year to show, but the app should present it as approximate, not exact.
After the Liberation of Mandalore, Din Djarin formally adopts him and his full name becomes Din Grogu (The Mandalorian season 3 finale). Wookieepedia uses Din Grogu as his article name.

notes.suggested: Affiliation: Jedi Order (former), Mandalorians / Clan Mudhorn; Adoptive father: Din Djarin; Masters: Kelleran Beq, Luke Skywalker, Din Djarin
notes.detail: The infobox lists these affiliations and masters. They are central to who he is.
Canon places the film's events 'years' after season 3 (after 9 ABY) but does not give an exact year. I dated them 'After 9 ABY'. Once reference material settles a year, place the film accordingly.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Bo-Kata.description: Bo-Katan Kryze spent decades fighting to free Mandalore, and she did it first as a terrorist, then as a rebel, and finally as its ruler. She was born into the royal House Kryze and grew up in the shadow of her pacifist sister, Duchess Satine. Rejecting Satine's New Mandalorian ideals, she joined Death Watch and became Pre Vizsla's trusted lieutenant and commander of the elite Nite Owls. She helped Vizsla and Maul's Shadow Collective overthrow her sister's government, then broke with Maul when he killed Vizsla and seized the throne. She rescued Satine too late to save her, freed Obi-Wan Kenobi, and led the resistance in the civil war that followed. Working with Ahsoka Tano, she brought the Republic's forces to Mandalore, captured Maul during the Siege of Mandalore and was named regent. She lost the position when she refused to serve the new Emperor and Clan Saxon betrayed her. Years later she helped Sabine Wren destroy the Duchess weapon and accepted the Darksaber to lead the clans against the Empire. Her rule ended in the Night of a Thousand Tears, when Moff Gideon took the blade from her. After the Empire fell she raided Imperial shipments, helped Din Djarin rescue Grogu and eventually won back the Darksaber. She then united the scattered Mandalorian coverts, retook Mandalore from Gideon's remnant forces and relit the Great Forge to begin rebuilding her homeworld.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Bo-Kata.socialDesc: Bo-Katan Kryze went from Death Watch lieutenant to Mand'alor, battling Maul and the Empire for the Darksaber before leading her people home to Mandalore.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Bo-Kata.timeline:
Unknown - Birth into House Kryze

Born on Mandalore into Clan Kryze, the royal house of Mandalore, as the younger sister of Satine Kryze. She grows up flying over the hills of Kalevala.

Unknown - Taking the Creed

As a child she recites the Mandalorian Creed in the Living Waters beneath Mandalore while her father, Adonai Kryze, watches. Later she dismisses the ceremony as theater for the royal family's subjects.

Unknown - Joining Death Watch

After her father dies and Satine becomes Duchess of the pacifist New Mandalorians, Bo-Katan joins Death Watch. She becomes Pre Vizsla's lieutenant and commander of the Nite Owls.

~21 BBY - Exile to Carlac

After Death Watch's failed alliance with Count Dooku, the group is exiled from the Mandalore system and sets up camp on Carlac.

20 BBY - Conflict on Carlac

She meets Lux Bonteri and his disguised companion, Ahsoka Tano, and fights Tano and a group of rebuilt battle droids when the Jedi's identity comes out.

19 BBY - Discovery of Maul

While Death Watch is based on Zanbar, she and Vizsla find Maul and Savage Opress drifting in an escape pod. Maul Force-chokes her when she questions an alliance with the Sith.

19 BBY - Forming the Shadow Collective

She joins the missions to Mustafar, Nal Hutta and Tatooine that bring Black Sun, the Pykes and the Hutts into Maul's Shadow Collective, and she leads the attack on Jabba's Palace.

19 BBY - Takeover of Mandalore

She helps stage Death Watch's fake rescue of Sundari, topples Satine's government, introduces Vizsla as Prime Minister and takes Maul prisoner.

19 BBY - Break with Maul

After Maul kills Vizsla in a duel for the Darksaber, she refuses to accept an outsider as ruler and escapes the palace with her loyal Nite Owls.

19 BBY - Rescue of Satine and Kenobi

With her nephew Korkie, she breaks Satine out of the royal prison, but Satine is recaptured. After Maul kills Satine, Bo-Katan frees Obi-Wan Kenobi and asks him to bring the Republic to Mandalore.

19 BBY - Hunting Maul

During the civil war she and the Nite Owls track Maul for months. She recruits Ahsoka Tano on Coruscant, and together they ask Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker for Republic help.

19 BBY - Siege of Mandalore

She fights alongside Tano and Rex's clone troopers, captures Prime Minister Almec and duels Gar Saxon. She helps take Maul prisoner and seals him in a Mandalorian vault.

19 BBY - Regent of Mandalore

The Jedi name her regent of Mandalore. When she refuses to obey the new Emperor, Clan Saxon betrays her and removes her from power during the Imperial occupation.

1 BBY - Destroying the Duchess

She allies with Clan Wren and the Spectres and helps Sabine Wren destroy the Arc Pulse Generator aboard Tiber Saxon's Star Destroyer.

1 BBY - Taking the Darksaber

With the backing of several clans, she accepts the Darksaber from Sabine and leads the Mandalorian resistance. The Children of the Watch reject her claim because she did not win the blade in combat.

Imperial Era - Night of a Thousand Tears

The Empire devastates Mandalore in the Great Purge. She surrenders to Moff Gideon, who betrays the ceasefire and takes the Darksaber from her.

9 ABY - Raid on Trask

With Koska Reeves and Axe Woves, she rescues Din Djarin and Grogu, then seizes an Imperial Gozanti cruiser loaded with weapons.

9 ABY - Assault on Gideon's Cruiser

She helps Djarin rescue Grogu and takes the bridge of Gideon's light cruiser. Djarin wins the Darksaber from Gideon, and she refuses to accept it from him as a gift.

9 ABY - Loss of her Fleet

Without the Darksaber, she loses the support of her followers. Axe Woves takes her fleet, and she withdraws alone to Kalevala.

9 ABY - Return to Mandalore

She guides Djarin through the ruins of Mandalore, saves him from a cyborg captor and sees a living mythosaur while bathing in the Living Waters.

9 ABY - Reclaiming the Darksaber

She joins the Armorer's covert of the Children of the Watch, wins back her Nite Owl fleet in battle and receives the Darksaber from Djarin.

9 ABY - Liberation of Mandalore

She leads the united Mandalorians in retaking the planet from Moff Gideon's Imperial remnant and relights the Great Forge to begin the reconstruction.

birth.source: The birth field in the Wookieepedia infobox is empty, and no canon source gives a birth year. She is already an adult Death Watch lieutenant and Nite Owl commander in 20 BBY, so she was clearly born well before 36 BBY.

death.source: The death field in the Wookieepedia infobox is empty. She is alive as Mand'alor after the liberation of Mandalore in 9 ABY (The Mandalorian season 3).

notes.detail: Canon gives no birth year, so keeping the guess flag is right. But 36 BBY would make her 16 in 20 BBY, and at that point she is already Pre Vizsla's right-hand lieutenant and commands the Nite Owls. She is plainly an adult and older than Ahsoka. She is also Satine's younger sister and a seasoned veteran by 9 ABY. A guess in the mid-40s BBY fits the portrayal better.

The Wookieepedia infobox lists both Kalevala and Mandalore as homeworlds. She was born on Mandalore, but Kalevala is House Kryze's home, where she grew up and later went into seclusion in The Mandalorian season 3.
She holds the title of Mand'alor twice: during the Imperial-era resistance, and again after she reclaims the Darksaber and liberates Mandalore in 9 ABY.

notes.suggested: Consider adding timeline markers for the 19 BBY Siege of Mandalore, the 1 BBY Darksaber handoff, and the 9 ABY liberation of Mandalore
notes.detail: These are the character's major turning points, and the article dates each of them.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wilhuff.description: Wilhuff Tarkin was the cold architect of the Empire's rule by terror and the man who turned the Death Star on Alderaan. He came from a hard-edged Eriaduan dynasty that trained its heirs as hunters, and he made his name early by brutally crushing pirates in the Seswenna. After service with the Republic's Judicial Forces he became governor of Eriadu under Sheev Palpatine's patronage. He joined the Republic Navy when the Clone Wars broke out. As a captain he survived capture and torture in the Citadel on Lola Sayu, and the ordeal left him with a lasting regard for Anakin Skywalker and deep contempt for Jedi generalship. Promoted to admiral and then Adjutant General, he prosecuted Ahsoka Tano for the Jedi Temple bombing and pushed for her execution. Under the Empire he helped replace the clone army with conscripts, became the first Grand Moff with authority over the Outer Rim, and hunted rebels on worlds like Lothal. He also took control of the Death Star project from Orson Krennic. Convinced that fear alone could hold the galaxy together, he destroyed Jedha City, Scarif and Alderaan. He was still sure of victory when Luke Skywalker destroyed the station over Yavin, killing him with it.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wilhuff.socialDesc: Wilhuff Tarkin rose from Eriadu governor to the Empire's first Grand Moff, ordered the Death Star to destroy Alderaan, and died when it exploded at Yavin.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wilhuff.timeline:
~64 BBY - Birth on Eriadu

Born into the wealthy and demanding Tarkin family, and raised in the family compound to value discipline and obedience.

48 BBY - Trials on the Carrion Plateau

At sixteen, he finishes his wilderness training under his grand-uncle Jova by outwitting a pack of predators at the Carrion Spike. His training then moves on to space combat and piloting.

46 BBY - Crushing Q'anah's Marauders

Serving with the Outland Regions Security Force, he works out the pattern of the pirate Q'anah's raids, captures her ship and sends her crew slowly into a sun.

~45 BBY - Judicial training and meeting Palpatine

He attends the Sullust Sector Spacefarers Academy, where he meets Senator Palpatine, who helps him get into the Judicial Academy. He is later credited with saving his team during a mission to Halcyon.

36 BBY - Leaves the Judicial Forces

He resigns his rank to go into politics, as Palpatine had once suggested.

~34 BBY - Governor of Eriadu

With Palpatine's backing he becomes governor, drives immigrant communities off Eriadu, and helps undermine Chancellor Valorum around the Eriadu Conference.

~24 BBY - Rejecting Dooku

Over a series of dinners he turns down Count Dooku's attempts to bring Eriadu into the Separatist cause, which was secretly a loyalty test set by Sidious. He then decides not to seek reelection.

22 BBY - Joins the Republic Navy

When the Clone Wars begin he enlists as a captain and carries out covert missions for Chancellor Palpatine.

21 BBY - Murkhana and Kamino

He commands the assault on Murkhana and is decorated after the Battle of Kamino.

20 BBY - Captured and rescued from the Citadel

He is captured with Even Piell while carrying half of the Nexus Route in his memory, and is tortured at the Citadel on Lola Sayu. A Jedi team rescues him, and he forms a mutual respect with Anakin Skywalker.

20 BBY - Admiral at Carida

Now an admiral, he survives the Separatist rhydonium attack on the station Valor and writes a scathing report on Jedi command.

20–19 BBY - Special Weapons Group

He joins the Strategic Advisory Cell's group overseeing the battle station project, which puts him in rivalry with Krennic, and he questions Galen Erso.

19 BBY - Prosecutor of Ahsoka Tano

He leads the military's investigation of the Jedi Temple bombing and is made Adjutant General. He prosecutes Ahsoka Tano and asks for the death penalty until Barriss Offee confesses.

19 BBY - Rise of the Empire

He stands with Palpatine at the Empire's founding and becomes a regional governor.

19–18 BBY - Project War-Mantle

With Vice Admiral Rampart he oversees the replacement of clones with conscripted stormtroopers, including the operation that destroys Tipoca City on Kamino.

~14 BBY - Grand Moff of the Outer Rim

He becomes the Empire's first Grand Moff and forms an unofficial triumvirate with the Emperor and Darth Vader.

5 BBY - Arrival on Lothal

He arrives on Lothal to deal with the Spectres, executes the officers who failed to stop them, and captures Kanan Jarrus.

1 BBY - Seizing the Death Star

He tests the superlaser on Jedha City, takes command of the station from Krennic, and destroys the Scarif base during the rebel raid.

1 BBY - Destruction of Alderaan

To make an example of the planet and pressure Princess Leia, he orders Alderaan destroyed.

1 BBY - Death at the Battle of Yavin

He refuses to evacuate and is killed when Luke Skywalker destroys the Death Star.

birth.source: Wookieepedia infobox: 'c. 64 BBY, Eriadu'. This matches the article's statement that he was sixteen in 48 BBY when he finished the Carrion Plateau trials (from the Tarkin novel).

death.source: Wookieepedia: died during the Battle of Yavin aboard the DS-1 Orbital Battle Station (A New Hope). Dated 1 BBY under the Galactic Atlas convention.

notes.detail: Wookieepedia gives the birth as 'c. 64 BBY'. The year is worked out from his age (16 in 48 BBY), not stated outright. A minor Tarkin-novel detail (designing ships 'at the age of 19' in the 46 BBY context) points to 65 BBY instead. 64 BBY is still the best figure, but consider labelling it approximate.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Maul.description: Maul was the Sith assassin who announced the return of the Sith to the Jedi after a thousand years of hiding. He then spent more than three decades feeding on his hatred for the Jedi, for Obi-Wan Kenobi and for the master who threw him away. Darth Sidious took him from his mother, Talzin, as a child and made him into a weapon.
