https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Zorii_B.description: Hidden behind a bronzium-finished helmet and a voice-masking vocoder, Zorii Bliss was the feared leader of the Spice Runners of Kijimi and one of the few people who knew Poe Dameron's past as a criminal. She grew up in the smuggling outfit her mother Zeva ran and fell for Poe when he joined as a teenager. Their relationship fell apart at the Kijimi summit, when he turned down her offer to take the gang over together and walked away. Zorii went on to take control of the Spice Runners herself. Years later, with the First Order occupying Kijimi, she was saving up to escape on a Y-wing she named the Comeuppance. When Poe came back with Rey, Finn, Chewbacca and C-3PO in search of the way to Exegol, she met him at blaster point. Rey's fighting skill won her over, and she took the group to the droidsmith Babu Frik and gave Poe a captain's medallion so he could board a Star Destroyer. She turned down his offer to join the Resistance, but she escaped Kijimi before a Xyston-class Star Destroyer destroyed the planet. She then flew the Comeuppance with Babu Frik at the Battle of Exegol and celebrated the victory on Ajan Kloss, sharing a knowing look with Poe across the crowd.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Zorii_B.socialDesc: Zorii Bliss, masked leader of Kijimi's Spice Runners and Poe Dameron's former partner, escaped her world's destruction to fly at the Battle of Exegol.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Zorii_B.timeline:
~0 BBY - Birth on Kijimi

Zorii is born into the Bliss family, sometime between 1 BBY and 1 ABY. Her mother Zeva leads the Spice Runners of Kijimi, taking over from Zarah Bliss.

~5 ABY - Joins the Spice Runners

While still young, Zorii joins her mother's spice-running crew on Kijimi.

~18 ABY - Meets Poe Dameron

Teenage pilot Poe Dameron joins the Spice Runners. He and Zorii start a romance.

~18 ABY - The Kijimi Summit

Zeva plans to wipe out rival families at a fake summit. Zorii, who also opposes her mother, asks Poe to take over the gang with her. He says no and leaves Kijimi, and her feelings for him turn to fury. She tells him never to come back.

Before 34 ABY - Leader of the Spice Runners

Zorii takes command of the Spice Runners and becomes feared by her enemies and respected by her crew.

~34 ABY - First Order Occupation

After the Battle of Crait, the First Order takes over Kijimi. Tired of the suffering she sees everywhere, Zorii buys a BTA-NR2 Y-wing for about 40,000 credits and names it the Comeuppance, planning to leave.

35 ABY - Reunion with Poe

Poe comes back to Kijimi with Resistance agents looking for Exegol. Zorii and her goons confront him, but Rey's skill impresses her and she agrees to help.

35 ABY - Babu Frik's Workshop

Zorii takes the group to the droidsmith Babu Frik, who unlocks the forbidden Sith translation in C-3PO's memory. On the rooftop she talks with Poe about the occupation, encourages him to keep fighting and briefly lifts part of her helmet.

35 ABY - The Captain's Medallion

Zorii warns the group that First Order troops are coming and gives Poe a captain's medallion, at great cost to herself, so he can get aboard the Steadfast. She turns down his offer to come with them and stays on Kijimi.

35 ABY - Escape from Kijimi

Darth Sidious orders Kijimi destroyed by a Xyston-class Star Destroyer's axial superlaser. Zorii gets away before the planet is obliterated.

35 ABY - Battle of Exegol

Zorii flies the Comeuppance with Babu Frik alongside the Resistance and the Citizens' Fleet against the Sith Eternal's Final Order fleet.

35 ABY - Victory on Ajan Kloss

Zorii joins the Resistance's victory celebration and shares a look with Poe across the crowd.

birth.source: Wookieepedia infobox: born 'Between 1 BBY–1 ABY'. 0 BBY is the midpoint of that sourced range.

death.source: No death recorded. She survives the Battle of Exegol and attends the celebration on Ajan Kloss in 35 ABY (The Rise of Skywalker).

notes.detail: Our guess of 0 now sits in the middle of a sourced canon range: Wookieepedia gives her birth as between 1 BBY and 1 ABY. The '(this is a guess)' label is still accurate, since canon gives a range rather than a single year. You could add a note that the range is sourced.
Wookieepedia says she is also known as Zorii Wynn. The name was introduced by the Poe Dameron: Free Fall excerpt and novel.

notes.current: Episode IX: The Rise of Skywalker
notes.detail: She has a major role in the novel Poe Dameron: Free Fall (2020), which covers her Spice Runner past with Poe and the Kijimi summit. Add it if the timeline plots novels.

notes.suggested: Affiliation: Spice Runners of Kijimi, Citizens' Fleet
notes.detail: The infobox lists her affiliations as Spice Runners of Kijimi and Citizens' Fleet. Her mother is Zeva Bliss.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dryden_.description: Dryden Vos is best known as the refined, lethal face of the Crimson Dawn syndicate, a crime lord who hosted the galaxy's elite aboard his yacht First Light while secretly answering to Maul. He rose through the underworld during the Clone Wars as a Crimson Dawn leader within Maul's Shadow Collective, and in the war's last days he got Maul's warning to go into hiding before the Empire took power. In the early Imperial years he offered the hunted former Sith a way off Janix in exchange for Maul removing Crimson Dawn's boss Rintero, then led the extraction himself under stormtrooper fire. He took over the syndicate as its public figurehead, but Maul stayed in control behind him. Vos bought the young Qi'ra, branded her with the syndicate's mark, trained her in Teräs Käsi and made her his top lieutenant. In 10 BBY, after Tobias Beckett's crew lost a coaxium shipment on Vandor, Vos sent them to raid the Kessel mines instead, a job that brought Han Solo into his orbit. When the deal fell apart over Savareen, Vos turned on Han, and Qi'ra killed him in his own study. She then used his signet ring to report his death to Maul, blamed it on Beckett, and took his place.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dryden_.socialDesc: Dryden Vos fronted Crimson Dawn for Maul, ran the coaxium job that pulled in Han Solo, and was killed aboard his yacht by his lieutenant Qi'ra in 10 BBY.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dryden_.timeline:
Clone Wars - Rising Star of Crimson Dawn

Serves as a leader in Crimson Dawn under Boss Rintero after the syndicate joins Maul's Shadow Collective. He becomes a lieutenant in the alliance.

19 BBY - Ordered into Hiding

Maul contacts him by hologram, along with Marg Krim of the Pyke Syndicate and Ziton Moj of Black Sun. Maul foresees the end of the Clone Wars and tells the syndicate leaders to go into hiding.

~17–13 BBY - Bargain with Maul

Crimson Dawn has abandoned Maul, who is now trapped on Janix. After the assassination of Marg Krim, Vos reaches Maul through Looti Vario. He offers Maul safe passage off Janix if Maul kills Rintero and makes Vos head of Crimson Dawn.

~17–13 BBY - Extraction from Janix

Vos flies in on a Crimson Dawn shuttle and shoots down an Imperial gunship. He holds off stormtroopers at the landing ramp until Maul and his allies are aboard, then escapes into hyperspace.

~17–13 BBY - Figurehead of Crimson Dawn

Replaces Rintero as Crimson Dawn's public leader but remains subordinate to Maul, whom he contacts through a holographic signet ring. He runs the syndicate from his yacht, the First Light, which holds his collection of antiquities.

After 13 BBY - Acquiring Qi'ra

Buys Qi'ra from Sarkin Enneb and brands her with the Crimson Dawn mark. He trains her in martial arts, including Teräs Käsi, and makes her his top lieutenant.

~10 BBY - Beckett's Debt

Pays Tobias Beckett a bonus for killing Aurra Sing. Beckett later owes Vos a shipment of coaxium.

10 BBY - Failure on Vandor

Beckett's crew fails to steal coaxium from an Imperial conveyex because Enfys Nest's Cloud-Riders intervene. Beckett and his new recruit, Han Solo, come to the First Light to face Vos.

10 BBY - The Kessel Plan

Vos threatens Beckett but is persuaded by Han and Qi'ra to back a raid on the Kessel spice mines for unrefined coaxium, despite the risk of angering the Pykes. Qi'ra goes with the crew.

10 BBY - Death on Savareen

Warned by Beckett, Vos confronts Han on Savareen. Vos believes the coaxium is fake, but it is the real shipment. He fights Han and then Qi'ra with his petars, and Qi'ra kills him in his study. She uses his ring to tell Maul that Beckett killed Vos and takes over his position.

birth.source: Wookieepedia's infobox leaves the birth field blank, and no canon source gives a birth year. He was already an adult syndicate leader by 19 BBY (The Clone Wars, "The Phantom Apprentice"), so he was born well before the Clone Wars.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: died 10 BBY aboard the First Light at Savareen, killed by Qi'ra in Solo: A Star Wars Story.

notes.current: Star Wars: Maul - Shadow Lord, Solo: A Star Wars Story
notes.suggested: Add Star Wars: The Clone Wars
notes.detail: Vos appears as a hologram in The Clone Wars Season 7 episode "The Phantom Apprentice" (19 BBY), when Maul orders the syndicate leaders into hiding. This was his animated debut.
Canon gives no birth year, so keeping this flagged as a guess is correct. 50 BBY fits the character, who was an adult 'rising star' Crimson Dawn leader by 19 BBY, but no source supports it.

Sources disagree on when Vos became head of Crimson Dawn. The Phantom Apprentice Episode Guide calls him a syndicate leader in 19 BBY, but Maul - Shadow Lord later established that Rintero led Crimson Dawn at the time and that Vos took his place after the Janix extraction. Wookieepedia dates that only to between 17 BBY and about 13 BBY.
The Wookieepedia infobox lists both affiliations. The entry doesn't track either one, and they are central to the character.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tech.description: Tech was the brains of Clone Force 99, the Bad Batch: a clone whose deliberate mutations gave him an extraordinary intellect, making him the squad's slicer, engineer, pilot of the Marauder and constant source of statistics nobody asked for. Late in the Clone Wars he helped uncover the Separatists' theft of Rex's battle algorithm on Anaxes, rescued Echo from the Techno Union on Skako Minor and helped turn the tide of the Republic's campaign. When Order 66 came, his inhibitor chip failed to activate. He was the first to work out why the regular clones had turned on the Jedi. Along with Hunter, Wrecker, Echo and the young clone Omega, he deserted the new Empire and left Crosshair behind. As fugitives and mercenaries working for Cid on Ord Mantell, he forged chain codes, raced riot racers, survived the destruction of Tipoca City and helped expose the Empire's secret clone program. Beneath his literal manner lay real loyalty, and he told Omega that thinking differently did not mean he felt any less. During a raid on the Imperial summit at Raven's Peak on Eriadu, Tech stayed behind on a failing tram line so his brothers could escape, and he fell to his death.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tech.socialDesc: Tech, the goggled genius of Clone Force 99, hacked and piloted the Bad Batch through the Clone Wars and desertion before sacrificing himself on Eriadu.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tech.timeline:
~32 BBY - Created on Kamino

Grown in Tipoca City as clone CT-9902 from Jango Fett's template. In Nala Se's private laboratory his mutations are enhanced, giving him an exceptional intellect.

~22-20 BBY - Clone Force 99

Serves as the computer, technology and weapons specialist of the experimental Bad Batch alongside Hunter, Wrecker and Crosshair, on missions across the war including Felucia.

19 BBY - Insurrection on Yalbec Prime

Helps the squad put down an insurrection before being redeployed to the struggling Anaxes campaign.

19 BBY - Battle of Anaxes

With Rex, Jesse and Kix, infiltrates a Separatist Cyber Center. There he discovers that Rex's strategy algorithm is being fed to the enemy from Skako Minor.

19 BBY - Rescue of Echo on Skako Minor

Talks to the Poletecs in their own language, tracks Echo's signal to Purkoll and disconnects him from the Techno Union's machinery. He then summons keeradaks so the group can escape.

19 BBY - Victory at Anaxes

Disguises Echo's transmissions aboard Admiral Trench's dreadnought, helping trick the Separatist fleet into defeat. He turns down the medals offered, and Echo joins the squad.

19 BBY - Kaller and Order 66

Fights alongside Depa Billaba and Caleb Dume on Kaller. When Order 66 is issued, his inhibitor chip fails to activate. He relays the order's meaning to his squad.

19 BBY - Rise of the Empire on Kamino

Explains to the squad how the regular clones' programming differs from theirs. He meets Omega and determines from her DNA that she is also an enhanced clone.

19 BBY - Onderon and desertion

Refuses Tarkin's order to kill Saw Gerrera's civilians. He breaks out of the Kamino brig with his squad and Omega, then flies the Marauder away while Crosshair stays loyal to the Empire.

19 BBY - Fugitives on Saleucami

Forges Imperial chain codes so Cut Lawquane's family can escape off-world. Omega chooses to stay with the Batch.

19 BBY - Ordo Moon and Pantora

Starts building an inhibitor chip scanner, makes repairs while an Ordo Moon dragon prowls outside, and scrambles the Marauder's signature on Pantora while Fennec Shand hunts Omega.

19 BBY - Mercenaries for Cid

Becomes a mercenary for Cid on Ord Mantell. He takes jobs across the galaxy, including piloting a riot racer to earn a coaxium payout.

19 BBY - Fall of Tipoca City

Returns to Kamino to rescue Hunter and survives the Empire's destruction of Tipoca City. The squad escapes with Nala Se's clone data.

~19-18 BBY - Life on the run

Keeps taking missions for Cid, and on one of them grows close to the pirate Phee Genoa. He finds the island world of Pabu as a possible refuge and helps Senator Riyo Chuchi investigate the Empire's treatment of clones.

18 BBY - Death on Eriadu

Infiltrates Raven's Peak during the Imperial summit to find Dr. Royce Hemlock and Crosshair. As the squad's tram fails, he cuts himself loose so his brothers can escape, and falls into the chasm below.

birth.source: Wookieepedia's infobox leaves the birth field empty. Canon gives no creation date for any Clone Force 99 member. Our -32 guess is plausible for a Jango Fett clone who is an adult by 22–19 BBY, and it is correctly flagged as a guess.

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: 'During or after 18 BBY, Eriadu'. He died in the Bombing of Raven's Peak during the Imperial summit on Eriadu, in The Bad Batch Season 2 finale ('The Summit' / 'Plan 99').

notes.detail: Wookieepedia gives the death as 'During or after 18 BBY', so 18 BBY is the earliest possible year rather than a precisely fixed one. Keeping -18 is reasonable, but it rests on the approximate dating of Season 2 (19–18 BBY). Season 3 did not bring Tech back; the 'Tech is alive' fan theories were not borne out.
Wookieepedia lists his operating number as CT-9902. It could be shown as a metadata fact or as the altTitle.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wrecker.description: Wrecker is the muscle and demolitions specialist of Clone Force 99, the "Bad Batch" of genetically deviant clones whose mutations made them better at particular jobs. His gave him enormous size and strength and an eager love of explosions. He came out of the Kaminoan cloning program with a scarred, clouded left eye from an early mission. He fought through the late Clone Wars alongside Hunter, Tech and Crosshair. At the Battle of Anaxes he lifted a burning gunship off Commander Cody. He helped rescue Echo from the Techno Union on Skako Minor, and Anakin Skywalker let him detonate a Separatist dreadnought. His squad's mutations shielded them from Order 66, and after refusing to follow the new Empire's orders they deserted Kamino with the young clone Omega. Wrecker became her protective big brother, even after his inhibitor chip briefly turned him against her before it was removed. Through years as fugitives and mercenaries he survived the destruction of Tipoca City, lost Tech on Eriadu, and helped Hunter storm Mount Tantiss to free Omega and the captive clone children. He then settled on Pabu, one of the few clones to find a peaceful life after the war.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wrecker.socialDesc: Wrecker, the Bad Batch's towering demolitions expert, resisted Order 66, fled the Empire with Omega, and helped free the clones held at Mount Tantiss.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wrecker.timeline:
Date unknown - Created on Kamino

Grown from Jango Fett's template as CT-9903. A cloning deviation gives him extraordinary size and strength, and he is placed in the experimental unit Clone Force 99 with Hunter, Tech and Crosshair.

Clone Wars - Eye injury

An early mission leaves his left eye scarred and clouded, but the injury barely slows him down.

19 BBY - Insurrection on Yalbec Prime

While the squad puts down an insurrection, Wrecker cuts off a Yalbec queen's stinger, and the male Yalbec swarm the team.

19 BBY - Battle of Anaxes

After their gunship is shot down, he lifts the wreck off a trapped Commander Cody. He then helps Captain Rex's team raid a Separatist Cyber Center and trace Admiral Trench's intelligence to a live signal.

19 BBY - Rescue of Echo on Skako Minor

He overcomes his fear of heights to storm Wat Tambor's tower and destroys the lab where Echo was held. He also holds back a tri-droid to protect the Poletec villagers.

19 BBY - Destruction of Trench's fleet

Anakin Skywalker hands him a detonator taken from the Invulnerable, and Wrecker destroys the Separatist fleet over Anaxes. Echo then joins the squad.

19 BBY - Order 66 on Kaller

After the squad rescues Depa Billaba's forces, he watches the clones turn on the Jedi. Unaffected by the order, he stalls troopers pursuing Caleb Dume.

19 BBY - Return to an Imperial Kamino

He meets Omega, starts a mess-hall brawl, and is tested with live fire in a combat simulation run for Tarkin.

19 BBY - Desertion

After refusing to kill Saw Gerrera's followers on Onderon, the squad is imprisoned. Wrecker breaks the cell wall and escapes with Omega, but a reprogrammed Crosshair shoots him in the shoulder during the escape.

19 BBY - Life as fugitives

He reunites with the Lawquanes on Saleucami, tears the Marauder free of its impound clamps, and survives a crash on the Ordo Moon. On Pantora, Fennec Shand knocks him out. The squad starts taking jobs for Cid on Ord Mantell.

19 BBY - Inhibitor chip activates

His chip, weakened by his head injuries, takes over during a mission, and he tries to kill Omega. Once he is subdued, the chip is removed on Kamino.

19 BBY - Fall of Tipoca City

While rescuing Hunter, he survives the Empire's bombardment of Tipoca City and escapes the sinking ruins with his squad.

~18 BBY - Loss of Tech

During a raid on an Imperial vault on Eriadu, Tech falls to his apparent death and Omega is captured by the Empire.

~18 BBY - Search for Omega

He and Hunter hunt for Omega while hiding on Pabu and dodging Imperial pursuit, eventually working alongside a changed Crosshair.

~18 BBY - Raid on Mount Tantiss

He joins the assault on Dr. Hemlock's facility on Wayland, which frees Omega and the imprisoned clone children.

Years later - Life on Pabu

Now living peacefully on Pabu with Hunter and Crosshair, he sees a grown Omega off as she leaves to join the rebellion.

birth.source: The Wookieepedia infobox leaves the birth field blank, and no canon source dates Wrecker's decanting. The 32 BBY guess only fits the general start of Clone Army production.

death.source: The Wookieepedia infobox leaves the death field blank. Wrecker survives Star Wars: The Bad Batch and is alive in the series finale's epilogue on Pabu.

notes.detail: Wookieepedia gives his clone designation as CT-9903. It works as the second identity, the way other clones carry their numbers.
Canon gives no birth year. Keeping -32 flagged as a guess is appropriate, since it only matches the general start of Clone Army production.

The article carries a Conflicting tag between the Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia: Join the Battle! and the Databank. It doesn't say which detail conflicts, but it probably concerns a physical or biographical detail, not dates. Later-season dating (Tech's death, the Tantiss raid, the Pabu epilogue) was not in the truncated excerpt, so those timeline years are approximate.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R4-P17.description: Obi-Wan Kenobi's loyal astromech through the last years of the Republic, R4-P17 was a cautious but quick-reacting droid with feminine programming, recognizable by the red replacement dome she wore on her white body. She rode in the socket of Kenobi's starfighter when he investigated the plot against Senator Padmé Amidala, which took them to Kamino and a dogfight with Slave I before they reached Geonosis. She stayed with him once the Clone Wars broke out. She fended off scavenging Jawas on Tatooine with her shock prod, flew his fighter by herself above Teth after he leapt into the battle below, and went with him on missions to Rodia and Mandalore. She was also with him when Asajj Ventress shot them down at Sullust. Her service ended in the war's final days during the Battle of Coruscant, when buzz droids swarmed Kenobi's interceptor near General Grievous's flagship and sawed off her dome before his warning could help. R4-G9 took her place for the mission to Utapau.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R4-P17.socialDesc: R4-P17, Obi-Wan Kenobi's red-domed astromech, flew with him from Kamino through the Clone Wars until buzz droids tore her apart above Coruscant.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R4-P17.timeline:
Before 22 BBY - Manufactured by Industrial Automaton

Built as an R4-P model astromech with feminine programming and later assigned to Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi. She wears a red dome taken from another astromech.

22 BBY - Mission to Kamino

Rides in the droid socket of Kenobi's Delta-7 starfighter while he traces the assassin who tried to kill Padmé Amidala, and helps him evade Jango Fett's Slave I.

22 BBY - Geonosis

Goes with Kenobi to Geonosis, where he uncovers the Separatist droid army just before the Clone Wars begin.

~22 BBY - Tatooine and Jabba's Palace

While guarding Kenobi's starfighter during talks with Jabba the Hutt, she shocks a Jawa with her prod and drives off the scavengers.

~22 BBY - Battle of Teth

Pilots Kenobi's starfighter on her own after he jumps from it to join the fight on the ground during the rescue of Jabba's son.

~21 BBY - Rodia

Travels with Kenobi to Rodia to stop Cad Bane from kidnapping Force-sensitive children.

~21 BBY - Mandalore

Goes with Kenobi to Mandalore, where he meets Duchess Satine Kryze. She stays behind while he goes to the Sundari Royal Palace.

~20 BBY - Battle of Sullust

Asajj Ventress shoots her and Kenobi down. They escape as the Separatist command ship is destroyed.

~19 BBY - Jedi Temple

Rolls through the Temple corridors alongside R4-M1 while Kenobi and Mace Windu discuss Yoda.

19 BBY - Destroyed at the Battle of Coruscant

Buzz droids land on Kenobi's Eta-2 interceptor as he approaches the Invisible Hand to rescue Chancellor Palpatine, and they saw off her dome before his warning can help.

19 BBY - Replaced by R4-G9

R4-G9 takes over as Kenobi's astromech for his mission to Utapau.

birth.source: The Wookieepedia infobox leaves the birth field empty. The article only says she was manufactured by Industrial Automaton sometime before the Clone Wars, and she first appears in 22 BBY (Attack of the Clones).

death.source: Wookieepedia infobox: died 19 BBY in the Coruscant system. She was destroyed by buzz droids during the Battle of Coruscant in Revenge of the Sith.

notes.suggested: Manufacturer: Industrial Automaton; Model: R4-P astromech droid
notes.detail: The Wookieepedia infobox lists the manufacturer as Industrial Automaton and the model as an R4-P astromech (R-series). These are more useful than a Homeworld of 'Unknown', since a droid has no homeworld.
The Wookieepedia infobox gives feminine programming and she/her pronouns.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Orson_C.description: Orson Krennic was the ambitious Imperial director who pushed the Death Star from a stalled Separatist blueprint to a working planet-killer, and died under its fire on Scarif. A gifted, charming architect, he met the scientist Galen Erso in the Republic Futures Program and later used that friendship for his own ends. During the Clone Wars he joined the secret Special Weapons Group, got the Erso family out of Separatist captivity on Vallt and brought the Geonosians in to build the station. Under the Empire he drew Galen into Project Celestial Power, claiming it was about clean energy while secretly turning his kyber research into a weapon. His career rose and fell with every setback and with his running feud with Wilhuff Tarkin. After the Ersos fled, Krennic tracked them to Lah'mu, where his death troopers killed Lyra and he took Galen back to finish the superlaser. In the Empire's last years before the Galactic Civil War, he set up the Ghorman project to seize kalkite, fought Grand Admiral Thrawn for funding and kept the project secret. In the end it got away from him. After he ordered the test that wiped out Jedha City, rebels stole the station's plans from Scarif. Tarkin took command of the Death Star and fired on the base, and Krennic died in the blast of the weapon he had spent his life building.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Orson_C.socialDesc: Orson Krennic drove the Death Star to completion for the Empire, exploiting his friend Galen Erso, only to die when Tarkin turned the station on Scarif.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Orson_C.timeline:
~51 BBY - Birth on Lexrul

Born in Sativran City on Lexrul in the final decades of the Galactic Republic.

36 BBY - Republic Futures Program

At fifteen, earns a place in the Futures Program on Brentaal, where he befriends fellow student Galen Erso. He graduates with high honors after becoming famous for his late nights out.

~30s BBY - Republic Corps of Engineers

Joins the design regiment of the Corps of Engineers and supervises large construction projects. He uses his influence to get Galen a visiting professorship at the Institute of Applied Science.

23 BBY - Kartoosh Facility

Helps engineer the huge construction and overhaul facility above Kartoosh.

~22 BBY - Strategic Advisory Cell

During the Clone Wars, secretly joins the Republic Special Weapons Group and argues that the Republic should build the captured battle station design itself, using Galen Erso's crystal research.

~22 BBY - Rescue on Vallt

Posing as a Zerpen Industries employee, trades captured Separatist scientists for the imprisoned Erso family. He then calls in a Republic cruiser, which destroys the Keep where they were held.

~22 BBY - The Geonosian Hive

Persuades the captive Archduke Poggle the Lesser to have his hive build the Death Star. Months later, Poggle orders his drones to tear down their work and escapes, badly damaging Krennic's reputation.

~19 BBY - Project Celestial Power

After the Empire replaces the Republic, recruits Galen for a supposed clean-energy program on Coruscant while secretly turning his kyber crystal research into a weapon.

~19 BBY - Malpaz Disaster

A weapons research facility on Malpaz explodes. Krennic covers it up as an attack to keep Galen working, and receives only a modest promotion to commander.

~18 BBY - Summit at Raven's Peak

Briefs Tarkin's summit on Eriadu about Project Stardust. Partisans and Clone Force 99 attack the compound during the meeting.

~18 BBY - Superlaser Prototype

While Tarkin is busy with an uprising in the Salient system, he test-fires a prototype weapon into the Hero Twins black holes.

~18 BBY - The Ersos Escape

With Saw Gerrera's help, the Erso family slips away from Coruscant. Krennic is demoted to lieutenant commander and vows to find them.

14 BBY - Tarkin Becomes Grand Moff

Tarkin gains authority over the Death Star but keeps his distance, blaming Stardust's setbacks on Krennic.

13 BBY - Lah'mu

Now Director of Advanced Weapons Research, he tracks the Ersos to Lah'mu. His death troopers kill Lyra after she wounds him, and he takes Galen back to finish the superlaser while Jyn escapes.

~9 BBY - Construction Moves to Scarif

After Saw Gerrera gets close to discovering the station, construction moves from Geonosis to Scarif. Brierly Ronan becomes Krennic's devoted assistant director.

~4 BBY - Maltheen Divide Conference

Reveals the Empire's need for Ghorman's kalkite and gives Dedra Meero control of the Ghorman project, which will stir up rebellion to justify a takeover.

3 BBY - Sculdun's Investiture Party

Trades barbs with Senator Mon Mothma at Davo Sculdun's party on Coruscant.

2 BBY - Ghorman Massacre

The Ghorman project ends in a massacre and full Imperial occupation, and strip-mining for kalkite begins on Krennic's timetable.

1 BBY - Imperial Ball

Attends the Empire Day ball, where a drunk subordinate leaks his interest in Jedha's kyber to a reporter.

1 BBY - Sev Tok Conference

Aboard the Firedrake, gets Thrawn to bet his TIE Defender funding on solving Stardust's gralloc supply problem, and sends Ronan to watch him.

1 BBY - Destruction of Jedha City

After a pilot defects with a message about the station, Tarkin takes over the project and fires the superlaser at Jedha City at Krennic's urging. Tarkin then credits himself with the success.

1 BBY - Mustafar and Eadu

Asks Darth Vader for an audience with the Emperor but is warned instead. On Eadu, he has Galen's engineers executed, and Galen is killed in the rebel air raid that follows.

1 BBY - Death on Scarif

Fails to stop Rogue One from sending the Death Star plans and is wounded by Cassian Andor. He dies on Scarif when Tarkin fires the station on the Citadel.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tynnra_.description: Tynnra Pamlo lived a double life in the Imperial Senate. She sat openly for Taris while secretly serving as Minister of Education in the Rebel Alliance's Civil Government. In the first days of the Empire she joined Bail Organa and Riyo Chuchi in fighting the Imperial Defense Recruitment Bill, arguing that the galaxy had more urgent needs than a costly new army. That effort collapsed when Palpatine used Admiral Rampart's destruction of Tipoca City as a reason to endorse the bill himself. In the years that followed, Pamlo worked with Rebel Intelligence and Airen Cracken. She gathered reports of Imperial atrocities and spread counterpropaganda, and she took part in the Organas' strategy dinners on Alderaan, which were disguised as social evenings. Although she opposed Palpatine, she was one of the Alliance's most cautious voices and would not drag her homeworld into open war. When Jyn Erso told the Alliance High Command about the Death Star, Pamlo argued for disbanding the Alliance rather than attacking Scarif, dismissing the plan as nothing but hope. After Rogue One went ahead anyway and the Galactic Civil War began, she returned to Coruscant, publicly condemned the battle station and resigned her Senate seat.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tynnra_.socialDesc: Tynnra Pamlo, Taris's senator and a secret Rebel Alliance minister, fought the Empire's army bill and opposed the Scarif raid before quitting the Senate.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tynnra_.timeline:
~18 BBY - Opposes the Defense Recruitment Bill

As senator for Taris in the new Imperial Senate, Pamlo joins Bail Organa in opposing Admiral Rampart's plan to replace the clone army with conscripts. She argues that the war is over and that the galaxy has more pressing problems.

~18 BBY - The vote is tabled

Pamlo and Organa get Mas Amedda to table the vote again until provisions for retiring clones are clearly defined.

~18 BBY - The Clone Conspiracy exposed

Pamlo watches in shock as Riyo Chuchi reveals footage of Rampart destroying Tipoca City. Palpatine then appears, has Rampart arrested and uses the scandal to endorse the Defense Recruitment Bill, which marks the start of the stormtrooper era.

Imperial Era - Secret rebel minister

While still in the Senate, Pamlo becomes Minister of Education in the Alliance's Civil Government. She works with Rebel Intelligence and Airen Cracken, collecting reports of Imperial atrocities on Lasan, Geonosis and Ghorman and producing counterpropaganda.

3 BBY - Leia Organa's Day of Demand

Pamlo attends Leia's Day of Demand ceremony on Alderaan, where Queen Breha thanks her personally for coming.

~3 BBY - Strategy dinners on Alderaan

Pamlo attends the Organas' dinner parties, which are secretly rebel strategy meetings. At one of them Grand Moff Tarkin arrives unexpectedly, and Breha stages a drunken scene to hide what the guests are really discussing.

1 BBY - Operation Fracture

Pamlo is part of the Alliance leadership that plans to extract Galen Erso. She and Organa intend to bring him before the Senate to testify about the Empire's weapon.

1 BBY - Council on Yavin 4

After hearing from Jyn Erso and Cassian Andor, Pamlo asks what chance the rebels have against a planet-killing weapon. She calls for the Alliance to disband and scatter, and she rejects the raid on Scarif because it rests on nothing but hope.

1 BBY - Resignation from the Senate

After Rogue One's unsanctioned attack on Scarif starts the Galactic Civil War, Pamlo returns to Coruscant, publicly condemns the Death Star and resigns her Senate seat.

birth.source: Wookieepedia's infobox has no birth date, and no canon source gives her age. Our 50 BBY guess is reasonable for someone already a senator by about 18 BBY, and it is correctly flagged as a guess.

death.source: Wookieepedia's infobox has no death date. Her last known act is resigning from the Imperial Senate around the Battle of Scarif (1 BBY), and canon does not say what happened to her after that.

notes.suggested: Affiliation: Imperial Senate (Taris); Rebel Alliance Civil Government (Minister of Education)
notes.detail: Wookieepedia says she was the Alliance Civil Government's Minister of Education and a member of Alliance High Command. This double role is the core of the character, and we don't track it yet.

Canon's last event for her is resigning from the Senate around 1 BBY. Nothing places her at or after Endor, so extending the column to 4 ABY is only a rendering choice. It is fine as long as it stays flagged unknown.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Crossha.description: Crosshair is the razor-eyed sniper of Clone Force 99, the "Bad Batch," whose mutated eyesight made him one of the deadliest marksmen in the Grand Army of the Republic. After fighting alongside his squad in the late Clone Wars, including the rescue of Echo on Skako Minor and the Battle of Anaxes, he alone among his brothers obeyed Order 66 on Kaller. Tarkin had his inhibitor chip strengthened, and he turned on his squad as they fled Kamino with the young clone Omega. He then led an Imperial Elite Squad against them on Onderon, Bracca and Ryloth, and kept serving the Empire even after his chip was removed. He killed his own squad to try to win his brothers back, but refused to leave with them when Tipoca City was destroyed. His faith in the Empire wore down over the next year. He watched clones like Cody desert, and after the Empire let his comrade Mayday die on Barton IV, he killed the officer responsible. That act sent him to a cell at Mount Tantiss, where Doctor Hemlock held him for months and questioned him about his old squad. He escaped with Omega, fought his way back into his brothers' trust despite a worsening tremor in his shooting hand, and helped destroy Tantiss. He finally settled on Pabu with the family he had once hunted.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Crossha.socialDesc: Crosshair, the Bad Batch sniper who obeyed Order 66, hunted his own brothers for the Empire, then broke free of Tantiss to rejoin Clone Force 99 on Pabu.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Crossha.timeline:
~32 BBY - Created on Kamino

Grown on Kamino as CT-9904, a clone of Jango Fett with mutations that gave him exceptional eyesight. He is assigned to the experimental unit Clone Force 99 as its sniper.

Clone Wars - Service with the Bad Batch

Fights in the Clone Wars with Hunter, Tech and Wrecker, looking down on regular "regs." The squad builds a near-perfect mission record and at some point meets Cut Lawquane's family on Saleucami.

19 BBY - Battle of Anaxes and Skako Minor

Deployed under Anakin Skywalker to Anaxes, where he clashes with Rex. He helps rescue Echo from the Techno Union on Skako Minor, then helps break the Separatist hold on Anaxes by boarding Admiral Trench's dreadnought.

19 BBY - Order 66 on Kaller

Alone among his squad, he tries to carry out Order 66, firing on the Padawan Caleb Dume until Dume knocks him out.

19 BBY - Rise of the Empire

Back on Kamino, he watches the Empire's proclamation, meets Omega and is tested by Tarkin. When he tries to massacre civilians on Onderon, his squad stops him.

19 BBY - Turns on Clone Force 99

Tarkin has his inhibitor chip strengthened. He fires on his former squad as they escape Kamino with Omega, wounding Wrecker.

19 BBY - Commander of the Elite Squad

Takes command of a squad of non-clone Imperial recruits. On Onderon he executes surviving insurgents and kills ES-01 for questioning his orders.

19 BBY - Burned on Bracca

Corners the Bad Batch in a wrecked Venator at the Bracca scrapyards, but is badly burned when they blow out an ion engine. The injury likely damages his inhibitor chip, which is later removed.

19 BBY - Occupation of Ryloth

Serves Vice Admiral Rampart on Ryloth. He shoots Orn Free Taa to frame Cham Syndulla, but fails to stop the Bad Batch from rescuing the Syndullas.

19 BBY - Destruction of Tipoca City

Lures his old squad to Kamino using the captured Hunter, then kills his own Elite Squad and reveals that his chip is gone. He saves Omega and AZI as Rampart sinks the city, but refuses to leave with his brothers and waits 32 rotations to be recovered.

~18 BBY - Mission to Desix

Once medically cleared, he deploys with Commander Cody and executes the Separatist holdout leader Tawni Ames. Cody's doubts, and his later desertion, stay with Crosshair.

18 BBY - Mayday's Death on Barton IV

Forms a bond with the neglected Clone Commander Mayday. When Lieutenant Nolan leaves Mayday to die, Crosshair kills Nolan and is taken into custody.

18 BBY - Prisoner of Tantiss

Held at Mount Tantiss on Wayland, where Doctor Royce Hemlock and Emerie Karr question him about the Bad Batch. Around this time a tremor develops in his shooting hand.

18 BBY - Escape with Omega

After Omega is captured and brought to Tantiss, the two escape together. They survive in the wilds and on the run before reuniting with Hunter and Wrecker, who reluctantly let him back into the squad.

18 BBY - Return to Tantiss

Helps free Omega and the captive clone children and bring down Hemlock's operation at Mount Tantiss. He plays a key part in the final battle despite his faltering hand.

After 18 BBY - Life on Pabu

Settles on Pabu with Hunter, Wrecker and Omega. Years later he is there to see a grown Omega leave to join the fight against the Empire.

birth.source: The Wookieepedia infobox leaves the birth field blank, and no canon source gives a creation date for any member of Clone Force 99. The Kamino lab scene in The Bad Batch confirms only that Omega is older than the squad. Our 32 BBY guess matches the general production window for the clone army and is reasonable as a placeholder.

death.source: The Wookieepedia infobox leaves the death field blank. Crosshair survives The Bad Batch and appears alive on Pabu in the series finale's epilogue.

notes.detail: Wookieepedia gives his operating number as CT-9904, and it is part of the article's title name. Other clone entries use altTitle for this kind of second identifier.
Canon never gives a creation year for Crosshair or any other Bad Batch member, so keeping 32 BBY flagged as a guess is correct. Do not remove the flag.

He is alive at the end of The Bad Batch. The finale epilogue, set some years after 18 BBY, shows him on Pabu when the adult Omega leaves, and no canon source shows him later or records his death. Leaving the column open is fine, but the last point canon places him is that epilogue, well before 0 BBY. If you prefer, the column could end around the epilogue rather than at 30 ABY.

notes.suggested: Affiliation: Galactic Republic (Clone Force 99), Galactic Empire (Elite Squad), later deserter/prisoner of Tantiss
notes.detail: His change of allegiance is the core of his arc and is not currently tracked.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wedge_A.description: Wedge Antilles is one of the Rebellion's great survivor pilots. He flew against both Death Stars and lived through both battles, and later helped train the next generation of Resistance flyers. He grew up flying and fixing ships on Corellia and first trained as a TIE fighter cadet at the Imperial Skystrike Academy. The Empire had hurt his family, friends and the girl he loved, and after an Imperial massacre of surrendering rebels he reached out to Fulcrum. In 2 BBY Sabine Wren got him and Hobbie Klivian out of the academy. He flew with Phoenix Squadron through the Battle of Atollon, then as Red Two at Yavin, where he and Luke Skywalker were the only members of Red Squadron to survive. At Hoth, flying as Rogue Three with gunner Wes Janson, he brought down the first AT-AT of the battle. He then rebuilt the Alliance's shattered fighter group as its commander and led Red Squadron at Endor, where he and Lando Calrissian destroyed the second Death Star. For the New Republic he was captured while scouting Akiva, formed Phantom Squadron to help liberate Kashyyyk, and fought at Jakku, the battle that ended the Empire. He then became a flight instructor, married Norra Wexley and settled on Akiva. Decades later he came out of retirement to fly with the Resistance at Exegol, but he arrived too late to save his stepson Temmin.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wedge_A.socialDesc: Wedge Antilles, the Imperial cadet turned Rebel ace, survived both Death Star runs, helped destroy the second, and flew again for the Resistance at Exegol.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Wedge_A.timeline:
Unknown - Youth on Corellia

Grows up on Corellia working at a fuel depot and on farms, learning to fly and repair ships. As a youth he chases down a pirate gunboat in a borrowed starfighter and destroys it.

Before 2 BBY - Imperial Cadet at Skystrike Academy

Recruited by the Empire while hauling cargo, he trains as a TIE pilot at Skystrike Academy on Montross, where he befriends Hobbie Klivian and Rake Gahree.

2 BBY - Defection to the Rebellion

After the Teralov massacre he contacts Fulcrum about defecting. Sabine Wren infiltrates the academy, and with Agent Kallus's help Wedge and Hobbie escape in a TIE bomber and join Phoenix Squadron at Chopper Base on Atollon.

2 BBY - Visit to Gahree's Family

Wedge and Hobbie try to honor their fallen friend's family, but Instructor Goran ambushes them there. They escape and realize they can never go home.

~1 BBY - Mission to Killun 71

Now an Alliance lieutenant, he poses as a TIE pilot to steal Imperial codes with AP-5 and Chopper. On the way back, Imperial slicers take control of Chopper.

1 BBY - Battle of Atollon

Flies an A-wing against Grand Admiral Thrawn's assault on Chopper Base and escapes with the survivors to Yavin 4.

1 BBY - Battle of Scarif Announcement

While grounded by an injury on Yavin 4, he tells rebel pilots over the base announcement system to redeploy to Scarif.

0 BBY - Battle of Yavin

Flies as Red Two, saves Luke Skywalker from a TIE fighter, and is forced out of the trench run by damage. He and Luke are the only Red Squadron survivors.

~0 ABY - Missions with Red Squadron

Continues flying under Arhul Narra, including the Giju evacuation and the hijacking of the Star Destroyer Harbinger to break the blockade of Tureen VII.

~2 ABY - Mercy Mission to Oulanne

As a lieutenant commander he leads a relief mission and recruits the former Imperial pilot Thane Kyrell into the Rebellion.

3 ABY - Battle of Hoth

As Rogue Three, he and gunner Wes Janson use a tow cable to bring down the first AT-AT of the battle, then help cover the evacuation.

3 ABY - Rebuilding Red Squadron

Promoted to commander, he gathers new pilots into a revived Red Squadron and wipes out a pirate base that threatens the fleet's rendezvous point.

~3 ABY - Operation Starlight

Flies with Shara Bey's Starlight Squadron to warn scattered fleet divisions that Alliance codes have been compromised.

4 ABY - Battle of Endor

Leads Red Squadron into the second Death Star's superstructure and, with Lando Calrissian, destroys its main reactor.

4 ABY - Captured on Akiva

Captured by Imperials while scouting their gathering on Akiva alone. He is freed during the uprising there alongside Norra Wexley and her allies.

5 ABY - Phantom Squadron and Kashyyyk

Forms Phantom Squadron and joins the unauthorized strike to liberate Kashyyyk, after which the squadron is disbanded.

5 ABY - Battle of Jakku

Leads the reformed Phantom Squadron at Jakku, the battle that finally defeats the Empire.

After 5 ABY - Flight Instructor and Marriage

Retires to teach at the New Republic's flight academy on Hosnian Prime, later marries Norra Wexley and settles on Akiva.

34 ABY - Recruited by the Resistance

Visited on Akiva by Poe Dameron, Temmin Wexley and Karé Kun, he agrees to help the struggling Resistance.

35 ABY - Battle of Exegol

Flies with Lando Calrissian and Chewbacca's Citizens' Fleet against the Final Order at Exegol. He arrives too late to save his stepson Temmin.

birth.source: The Wookieepedia infobox leaves the birth field empty, and no canon source dates his birth. The 21 BBY figure comes from Legends.

notes.detail: Canon gives no birth year. 21 BBY matches the Legends date, so keeping the guess flag is correct. It fits canon, since he is a young adult cadet in 2 BBY in Rebels.

https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mas_Ame.description: Mas Amedda was the bureaucrat who stood at Palpatine's shoulder through the Republic's final years and then helped run the Empire that replaced it. As Vice Chair and Speaker of the Senate under Finis Valorum, he slowed relief for Naboo during the 32 BBY blockade and steered the chancellor into the missteps that led to his ouster. He then pledged himself to Palpatine, who later told him he was secretly the Sith Lord Darth Sidious. In 22 BBY Amedda nudged Jar Jar Binks into proposing the emergency powers that created the Grand Army of the Republic. During the Clone Wars he ran the secret Strategic Advisory Cell, which oversaw the early Death Star project and Orson Krennic's rise. He also managed the Senate floor for Palpatine, pushing the attempted occupation of Mandalore and the bank deregulation and clone funding bills. When the Empire was declared he stayed at Palpatine's side and presided over the burning of fallen Jedi's lightsabers, then served as Grand Vizier and ran the huge Imperial bureaucracy. After Palpatine died at Endor, Amedda was left as a powerless figurehead under Gallius Rax. Once the Empire collapsed at Jakku, he signed its surrender to the New Republic and stayed on as the nominal head of Coruscant's provisional government. History remembers him as a spineless sycophant.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mas_Ame.socialDesc: Mas Amedda, Palpatine's loyal Speaker of the Senate, rose to Grand Vizier of the Empire and survived its fall to sign the surrender to the New Republic.
https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Mas_Ame.timeline:
32 BBY - Vice Chair Under Valorum

As Vice Chair and Speaker of the Senate, Amedda uses his bureaucratic power to slow relief for blockaded Naboo. Rumors say he is on the Trade Federation's payroll.

32 BBY - Valorum's Downfall

During Queen Amidala's appeal to the Senate, Amedda tells Valorum to sustain Lott Dod's objection. The advice helps provoke the Vote of No Confidence that removes Valorum from office.

32 BBY - Palpatine's Vice Chair

Amedda keeps his post after Palpatine is elected Supreme Chancellor and swears loyalty to him. Palpatine later reveals that he is Darth Sidious, and Amedda willingly joins his scheme.

~24 BBY - Strength and Unity Controversy

Amedda comes up with the Loyalist Committee's "Strength and Unity" propaganda poster. Because it includes his own image, the press accuses him of narcissism.

22 BBY - Emergency Powers

After the Separatists' droid army is revealed, Amedda talks Jar Jar Binks into proposing emergency powers for Palpatine, which lets the chancellor activate the clone army.

22 BBY - Launch of the Grand Army

Amedda stands with Palpatine and the Loyalist Committee to watch the clone army deploy after the First Battle of Geonosis.

22 BBY - Strategic Advisory Cell

Palpatine puts Amedda in charge of the Strategic Advisory Cell, the council that oversees the Republic's most secret military projects. One of his recruits is Orson Krennic.

~22 BBY - Zillo Beast Incident

Amedda backs Palpatine's decision to kill the Zillo Beast so it can be studied. The creature breaks loose and rampages across Coruscant.

21 BBY - Death Star Project

Amedda and Palpatine show the Cell the captured battle station plans. Amedda coordinates the project's early stages and reluctantly approves Krennic's plan to recruit Galen Erso.

~21 BBY - Mandalore Resolution

Amedda pushes the Senate to authorize an occupation of Mandalore over Duchess Satine Kryze's objections. The resolution is rescinded once Deputy Minister Jerec's undoctored testimony comes out.

~21 BBY - Pantora Blockade Hearings

Amedda presides over the Senate sessions on the Trade Federation's blockade of Pantora.

~20 BBY - Banking Deregulation and Clone Funding

Amedda helps defeat the Separatist peace initiative. He pushes through bank deregulation and Halle Burtoni's bill to buy five million more clones.

~20 BBY - Death of Onaconda Farr

Amedda attends Senator Farr's funeral and follows Inspector Tan Divo's investigation, which ends with Lolo Purs arrested for the murders.

20 BBY - Festival of Light

Amedda goes with Palpatine to Naboo, where Moralo Eval's bounty hunters try to kidnap the chancellor.

19 BBY - Rise of the Empire

Amedda is at Palpatine's side when the Empire is declared. He is present when Yoda confronts Sidious in the Senate chamber.

19 BBY - Burning of the Lightsabers

Amedda presides over a ceremony outside the burned Jedi Temple in which the lightsabers of fallen Jedi are destroyed.

19 BBY - Grand Vizier

Rewarded for his loyalty, Amedda becomes Grand Vizier and sits on the Imperial Ruling Council. He runs the Empire's bureaucracy from Coruscant and sometimes Byss.

4 ABY - Death of the Emperor

After Palpatine dies at Endor, Amedda is left as a powerless mouthpiece for the civilian government, controlled by Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax.

5 ABY - Surrender of the Empire

After the Battle of Jakku, Amedda signs the Galactic Concordance on Chandrila, surrendering the Empire to the New Republic.

5 ABY - Provisional Government

Amedda stays on as the nominal, powerless head of Coruscant's provisional government while the New Republic restores democracy.

birth.source: Wookieepedia's infobox leaves the birth field blank, and no canon source gives a birth year. He was already an adult and Vice Chair in 32 BBY, so our flagged guess of 70 BBY is plausible but has no source.

death.source: Wookieepedia's infobox leaves the death field blank. He was last known alive after the 5 ABY Galactic Concordance, as nominal head of Coruscant's provisional government (Aftermath: Empire's End). No canon death is recorded.

notes.detail: He is widely known by his Imperial title of Grand Vizier. Before that he was Vice Chair and Speaker of the Senate.

The column end of 9 ABY is fine as a rendering bound. His last documented canon activity is 5 ABY: he signed the Galactic Concordance and led Coruscant's provisional government (Aftermath: Empire's End). If the column is meant to track his last known appearance, 5 ABY is the accurate year.

notes.suggested: Track his role in the Aftermath trilogy (4–5 ABY) and in Catalyst (Strategic Advisory Cell, Death Star project)
notes.detail: The major post-Endor chapter of his story (figurehead under Gallius Rax, then surrender at Chandrila) is only in the novels, so none of our screen seenIn entries covers it.
